title: chore: add GitHub Actions workflows, PHPCS config, and WordPress Playground
body:
## Summary

Adds CI/CD infrastructure and developer tooling inspired by [wp-plugin-starter-template-for-ai-coding](https://github.com/wpallstars/wp-plugin-starter-template-for-ai-coding).

### GitHub Actions Workflows

- **tests.yml** - Runs on push/PR to main:
  - PHPUnit tests (PHP 8.2, 8.3 matrix)
  - PHPCS with WordPress coding standards
  - PHPStan static analysis

- **release.yml** - Triggered on version tags (`v*`):
  - Builds production assets (npm + composer)
  - Creates ZIP file for distribution
  - Publishes GitHub Release with auto-generated notes

- **code-quality.yml** - Runs on push/PR to main:
  - ESLint for JavaScript
  - Stylelint for CSS
  - Build verification

### PHPCS Configuration

- WordPress coding standards with PSR-4 adaptations
- Excludes vendor, node_modules, build, tests directories
- Allows camelCase method names (PSR convention)
- Allows PSR-4 class file naming
- PHP 8.2+ compatibility checks

### WordPress Playground

- `playground/blueprint.json` - Test latest release instantly in browser
- `playground/blueprint-dev.json` - Test development branch
- Links added to README for easy access

### Composer Scripts

```bash
composer phpcs      # Run PHP CodeSniffer
composer phpcbf     # Auto-fix PHPCS issues
composer phpstan    # Run static analysis
composer test       # Run PHPUnit tests
composer lint       # Run all linters
```

### README Updates

- Added CI status badges
- Added WordPress Playground links
- Updated development section with new commands

title: fix: resolve critical security and correctness issues in install-wp-tests.sh
body:
## Summary

- **Security (critical)**: Remove `set -x` xtrace to prevent `DB_PASS` credential exposure in CI logs — `mysqladmin` and `mysql` commands with `--password` were being echoed to stderr on every run
- **Correctness (high)**: Fix `wp-tests-config.php` existence check to use `$WP_TESTS_DIR/wp-tests-config.php` instead of `./wp-tests-config.php` — wrong path caused stale configs to block setup regeneration
- **Correctness (critical)**: Fix `recreate_db no` → `recreate_db yes` so the existing test DB is actually dropped when reinitializing — the previous code printed "Reinitializing will delete the existing test database" but then passed `no`, leaving stale tables and causing flaky tests

## Changes

`bin/install-wp-tests.sh`:
- Line 54: `set -ex` → `set -e`
- Line 115: `if [ ! -f wp-tests-config.php ]` → `if [ ! -f "$WP_TESTS_DIR/wp-tests-config.php" ]`
- Line 170: `recreate_db no` → `recreate_db yes`

Closes #4

title: fix: remove incorrect EscapeOutput.OutputNotEscaped global exclusion from phpcs.xml
body:
## Summary

- Removes the global `<exclude name="WordPress.Security.EscapeOutput.OutputNotEscaped"/>` from `phpcs.xml`
- The exclusion was mislabelled as "Allow file includes with variables (autoloader)" — `EscapeOutput.OutputNotEscaped` is the XSS/output-escaping sniff, entirely unrelated to file inclusion
- The `$asset = require $asset_file` pattern in `AdminPage.php`, `FloatingWidget.php`, and `Settings.php` does **not** trigger this sniff; the exclusion was never needed
- Re-enabling the sniff globally produces **zero new violations** (verified: `vendor/bin/phpcs --standard=phpcs.xml` passes clean)

## Verification

```
vendor/bin/phpcs --standard=phpcs.xml includes/ ai-agent.php
....... 7 / 7 (100%)
Time: 2.43 secs; Memory: 4MB
```

No violations with the XSS output-escaping check now active.

## Root cause

The original exclusion was added with an incorrect comment. `WordPress.Security.EscapeOutput.OutputNotEscaped` detects unescaped output in `echo`/`print`/`_e()` calls — it has no relationship to `include`/`require` file-inclusion patterns. Disabling it globally removed a high-signal XSS check for no benefit.

Closes #5

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Chores**
  * Enhanced code quality and security by enabling stricter output escaping validation checks in the development tooling.

title: t008: Make CI workflows non-continue-on-error
body:
## Summary

- Removes `continue-on-error: true` from the **ESLint** step in `code-quality.yml`
- Removes `continue-on-error: true` from the **Stylelint** step in `code-quality.yml`

These flags caused linter failures to be silently swallowed — the workflow showed green even when ESLint or Stylelint found violations. Removing them means linter failures now correctly fail the CI check, enforcing code quality gates on every PR and push.

No other workflows were affected: `tests.yml` has no `continue-on-error` flags, `release.yml` has none, and the `|| true` patterns in `issue-sync.yml` are intentional operational resilience for sync steps (not quality gates).

Closes #27

title: t007: Add pre-commit hooks via husky + lint-staged for PHP/JS/CSS
body:
## Summary

- Install **husky v9** and **lint-staged v16** as devDependencies
- Add `prepare` script so hooks are installed automatically on `npm install`
- Configure `lint-staged` in `package.json` to run linters only on staged files:
  - **JS/JSX** (`src/**/*.{js,jsx}`): `wp-scripts lint-js --fix`
  - **CSS** (`src/**/*.css`): `wp-scripts lint-style --fix`
  - **PHP** (`**/*.php`): `composer phpcbf --` (auto-fix) then `composer phpcs --` (check)
- Add `.husky/pre-commit` hook that runs `npx lint-staged`

## Behaviour

On every `git commit`, only the staged files are linted (not the whole codebase), keeping the hook fast. PHP files are auto-fixed by phpcbf first; if phpcs still finds violations after the fix, the commit is blocked.

## Verification

```bash
npm install          # triggers prepare → husky installs hooks
git add src/foo.js   # stage a JS file
git commit -m "test" # pre-commit hook runs lint-staged on foo.js only
```

Closes #26

title: t006: Fix npm audit vulnerabilities (26 issues: 12 moderate, 14 high)
body:
## Summary

- Resolves all 26 npm audit vulnerabilities (12 moderate, 14 high) by adding `overrides` in `package.json` to pin vulnerable transitive dependencies to patched versions
- Bumps `@wordpress/scripts` from `^31.2.0` to `^31.6.0` (latest)
- Build verified: `webpack 5.105.3 compiled successfully` with no new errors

## Vulnerabilities Fixed

| Package | Severity | Advisory | Fix |
|---------|----------|----------|-----|
| `ajv` | moderate | GHSA-2g4f-4pwh-qvx6 (ReDoS via `$data`) | `^8.18.0` |
| `flatted` | high | GHSA-25h7-pfq9-p65f (unbounded recursion DoS) | `^3.4.0` |
| `immutable` | high | GHSA-wf6x-7x77-mvgw (Prototype Pollution) | `^5.1.5` |
| `minimatch` | high | GHSA-3ppc-4f35-3m26, GHSA-7r86-cg39-jmmj (ReDoS) | `^9.0.7` |
| `serialize-javascript` | high | GHSA-5c6j-r48x-rmvq (RCE via RegExp.flags) | `^7.0.4` |
| `svgo` | high | GHSA-xpqw-6gx7-v673 (Billion Laughs DoS) | `^3.3.3` |
| `webpack-dev-server` | moderate | GHSA-9jgg-88mc-972h, GHSA-4v9v-hfq4-rm2v (source code theft) | `^5.2.3` |
| `yauzl` | moderate | GHSA-gmq8-994r-jv83 (off-by-one error) | `^3.2.1` |

## Approach

Used npm `overrides` (not `--force` downgrade) to pin transitive deps to safe versions. This is the correct approach — `npm audit fix --force` would have *downgraded* `@wordpress/env` to 10.38.0, which is the wrong direction.

## Verification

```
$ npm audit
found 0 vulnerabilities

$ npm run build
webpack 5.105.3 compiled with 3 warnings in 6811 ms
```

(Warnings are pre-existing bundle size warnings, not new issues.)

Closes #25

title: t009: Tighten PHPCS — re-enable EscapeOutput, add NonceVerification rules
body:
## Summary

- Re-enables `WordPress.Security.EscapeOutput` (both `OutputNotEscaped` and `ExceptionNotEscaped` sub-sniffs) by removing the two blanket exclusions that were added as temporary scaffolding
- Adds an explicit `WordPress.Security.NonceVerification` rule so future superglobal access without nonce checks is caught at lint time
- Adds one targeted `phpcs:ignore` on `FileAbilities.php:403` for a PHPCS false positive (ErrorException constructor arguments flagged as unescaped output)

## Verification

```
vendor/bin/phpcs --standard=phpcs.xml --report=full
# 7/7 files, 0 errors, 0 warnings
```

## Why the blanket exclusions were wrong

`EscapeOutput.OutputNotEscaped` was excluded with the comment "Allow file includes with variables (autoloader)" — but file includes are not output. The exclusion was silencing a real security sniff across the entire codebase. `EscapeOutput.ExceptionNotEscaped` was excluded with "Allow exception messages without escaping (internal use)" — also too broad; exception messages can contain user-controlled data.

The only legitimate false positive in the codebase is `FileAbilities.php:403` where `ErrorException` constructor arguments are misidentified as output. That is now suppressed with a targeted inline ignore and a clear rationale comment.

Closes #28

title: t012: Set up wp-env based test runner for local and CI
body:
## Summary

- Replaces the hardcoded `docker-compose -f ~/wp-env/<hash>/docker-compose.yml` path in `test:php` scripts with `wp-env run tests-wordpress` — portable across machines, no hash dependency
- Adds `test:php:testdox` and `test:php:coverage` npm scripts
- Mounts `tests/mu-plugins` into the wp-env tests environment via the `mappings` key in `.wp-env.json`
- Rewrites the CI `phpunit` job in `tests.yml` to use wp-env instead of the manual MySQL service + `svn` + `install-wp-tests.sh` approach; adds `wp-env:stop` cleanup step with `if: always()`
- Updates `CONTRIBUTING.md` with development setup and test-running instructions

## Local usage

```bash
npm run wp-env:start   # start environment (Docker required)
npm run test:php       # run PHPUnit inside wp-env
npm run test:php:testdox
npm run wp-env:stop
```

## Why wp-env over the old approach

The previous `test:php:docker` script embedded a content-addressed hash (`dffbc78ef1978dc39a48a06e0f171d9b`) from a specific local wp-env instance. This hash changes whenever `.wp-env.json` changes and is machine-specific — it would never work on CI or another developer's machine. `wp-env run` resolves the correct container automatically.

Closes #31

title: t029: Standardize error handling — return WP_Error not arrays with 'error' key
body:
## Summary

- Replaces all `return ['error' => '...']` patterns in ability handlers and tool executors with `new WP_Error(...)` objects
- Updates return type hints from `array` to `array|\WP_Error` on all affected handler methods
- Adds `/* translators: */` comments for all `sprintf(__())` calls with placeholders (PHPCS compliance)

## Why

The WordPress Abilities API resolver (`class-wp-ai-client-ability-function-resolver.php`) already converts `WP_Error` returns to `['error' => ...]` for the AI model, so this change is transparent to the model. Returning `WP_Error` is the idiomatic WordPress pattern per the project's own AGENTS.md rule: _"Return `WP_Error` objects; never throw exceptions in hooks"_.

## Files changed

**Abilities** (7 files):
- `KnowledgeAbilities` — `handle_knowledge_search`
- `MemoryAbilities` — `handle_memory_save`, `handle_memory_delete`

title: t044: Support all three official AI providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google)
body:
## Summary

- Add direct API key support for OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google AI — no WordPress AI Experiments plugin required
- New **Providers** settings tab with save/test/remove per provider
- AgentLoop routes to native provider APIs when `provider_id` is `openai`, `anthropic`, or `google`

## Changes

### PHP

**`Settings.php`**
- `DIRECT_PROVIDERS` constant — metadata + model lists for all three providers
- `PROVIDER_KEYS_OPTION` — dedicated wp_options key for credentials (never exposed via GET /settings)
- `get_provider_key(id)` / `set_provider_key(id, key)` — secure credential storage
- `get_configured_direct_providers()` — returns provider list with `has_key` status

**`AgentLoop.php`**
- `send_prompt_openai()` — calls `api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions`
- `send_prompt_anthropic()` — calls `api.anthropic.com/v1/messages` (Anthropic format: system as top-level field, tool_use/tool_result content blocks)
- `send_prompt_google()` — calls Google's OpenAI-compatible endpoint at `generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/openai/`
- `build_openai_messages()` / `build_openai_tools()` — shared helpers (also refactors `send_prompt_direct()` to use them)
- `send_prompt()` routes to the correct method based on `provider_id`

**`RestController.php`**
- `POST /ai-agent/v1/settings/provider-key` — save/clear an API key
- `POST /ai-agent/v1/settings/provider-key/test` — test a key with a minimal prompt
- `GET /ai-agent/v1/settings` — now includes `_provider_keys` map (boolean per provider, no values)
- `GET /ai-agent/v1/providers` — directly-configured providers listed first, WP SDK providers appended (deduped)

### JavaScript

- `src/settings-page/providers-manager.js` — new `ProvidersManager` component with per-provider cards (save/test/remove)
- `src/settings-page/settings-app.js` — new **Providers** tab as first tab; imports `ProvidersManager`
- `src/settings-page/style.css` — provider card styles

## Testing

1. Go to **Tools > AI Agent Settings > Providers**
2. Enter an OpenAI/Anthropic/Google API key and click **Save Key**
3. Click **Test Connection** — should show the model name on success
4. Select the provider in the chat header and send a message
5. Verify the response comes from the correct provider

title: t010: Raise PHPStan level from 5 to 6, fix new errors
body:
## Summary

- Raises PHPStan static analysis level from 5 to 6 in `phpstan.neon`
- Adds typed array annotations to 37 PHP files to satisfy level 6 `missingType.iterableValue` checks
- Adds `@return` type annotations to 3 REST controller methods that had no return type

## Changes

All 271 level-6 errors were `missingType.iterableValue` — PHPStan requiring value types on `array` parameters and return types. Fixed by adding precise PHPDoc types:

- `array<string, mixed>` for associative arrays (tool inputs, settings, context maps)
- `list<mixed>` for integer-indexed lists (hook args from `func_get_args()`)
- `list<array<string, mixed>>` for lists of structured arrays (blocks, chunks, triggers)
- `list<string>` for lists of strings (buffer lines, table rows, sentences)
- `array{float, float}|null` for `CostCalculator::get_pricing()` (tuple return)
- `array<string, bool>`, `array<string, int>`, `array<string, string>` for typed maps
- `WP_REST_Response|WP_Error` return types on 3 REST memory handler methods

Verified: `vendor/bin/phpstan analyse --no-progress` → **0 errors** at level 6.

Closes #29

title: t041: Add Abstract_Ability base class for OOP ability pattern
body:
## Summary

- Introduces `AiAgent\Abstracts\Abstract_Ability` — a `WP_Ability` subclass that mirrors the `Abstract_Ability` interface from the [WordPress/ai experiments plugin](https://github.com/WordPress/ai)
- Existing static `*Abilities` registrar classes are **unchanged** — full backward compatibility preserved
- The new pattern is purely additive; no existing code is modified

## What changed

**New file:** `includes/Abstracts/Abstract_Ability.php`

Concrete abilities extend this class and implement nine abstract methods:

| Method | Purpose |
|--------|---------|
| `ability_name()` | Fully-namespaced ability name (e.g. `my-plugin/do-something`) |
| `ability_label()` | Human-readable label (translated) |
| `ability_description()` | Detailed description (translated) |
| `ability_category()` | Category slug |
| `input_schema()` | JSON Schema for input |
| `output_schema()` | JSON Schema for output |
| `execute_callback($input)` | Core execution logic |
| `permission_callback($input)` | Permission check |
| `meta()` | Annotations + show_in_rest |

Then call `$ability->register()` inside `wp_abilities_api_init`.

## Design decisions

- **Method naming**: Uses `ability_*` prefix for abstract interface methods to avoid conflicts with `WP_Ability`'s public getters (`get_label`, `get_description`, `get_category`)
- **Constructor signature**: Matches `WP_Ability(string $name, array $args)` so `WP_Abilities_Registry` can instantiate subclasses via `ability_class` without modification. The registry-supplied args are intentionally ignored — subclass methods are the authoritative source
- **No compat layer changes**: `Abstract_Ability` lives in `includes/Abstracts/` and is autoloaded via PSR-4. It extends `WP_Ability` which is provided by either WordPress core (7.0+) or the compat layer

## Verification

```

PHPCS WordPress:  0 errors (includes/)
```

title: fix: update WP-CLI in Docker image before wp-env start
body:
## Summary

- Fixes the `PHPUnit (wp-env)` CI job that fails on every PR with `Error while running docker compose command` / empty `Error:` from WP-CLI
- Root cause: `wordpress:cli-php8.2` base image ships with WP-CLI < 2.8.0, which emits `Deprecated: trim(): Passing null` on PHP 8.2 and then exits with an empty `Error:` during `wp core multisite-install`
- Fix: add a CI step that patches the local `wordpress:cli-php8.2` image with the latest WP-CLI phar **before** `wp-env start` builds its CLI container from it

## How it works

wp-env generates a `cli` Dockerfile that starts with `FROM wordpress:cli-php8.2`. By patching the local image tag before `wp-env start`, the generated container inherits the updated WP-CLI binary. The patch step:

1. Pulls the latest `wordpress:cli-php8.2` from Docker Hub
2. Builds a thin layer on top that replaces `/usr/local/bin/wp` with the latest WP-CLI phar
3. Tags the result as `wordpress:cli-php8.2` locally — wp-env uses this local tag

## Why not other approaches

- **Update `/usr/local/bin/wp` on the CI runner host**: wp-env runs WP-CLI inside Docker containers, not on the host — this has no effect
- **`lifecycleScripts.afterStart`**: runs after setup completes; setup is what's failing, so this is too late
- **Pin `@wordpress/env` version**: fragile, ties CI to a specific version and doesn't address the root cause

## Affected PRs

Unblocks: #85, #90, #91, #92, #93, #94, #164

Closes #165

title: t050: Add event/hook system for ability execution (before/after hooks)
body:
## Summary

- Adds `execute_abilities_with_hooks()` private method to `AgentLoop` that wraps all ability execution with WordPress action/filter hooks
- Both call sites (`run_loop` and `resume_after_confirmation`) now route through the new wrapper
- Enables third-party plugins to observe, log, or modify ability execution without patching core

## Hooks Added

### `ai_agent_before_ability` (action)
Fires immediately before each ability is executed.
```php
do_action( 'ai_agent_before_ability', string $ability_name, array $params );
```

### `ai_agent_after_ability` (action)
Fires immediately after each ability has been executed.
```php
do_action( 'ai_agent_after_ability', string $ability_name, array $params, mixed $result );
```

### `ai_agent_ability_result` (filter)
Filters the result of an ability execution before it is returned to the model.
```php
$result = apply_filters( 'ai_agent_ability_result', mixed $result, string $ability_name, array $params );
```

## Implementation Notes

- Ability names are resolved from the SDK's `wpab__` function-name format back to the registered `namespace/name` format (e.g. `ai-agent/memory-save`) before hooks fire
- Response parts are paired with pending calls by position to correlate results with their originating call
- All three hooks include full PHPDoc blocks

## Quality Checks

- PHPStan level 5: **0 errors**
- PHPCS: **0 errors**

t037: Add per-tool WordPress capabilities (ai_agent_tool_{name})
body:
## Summary

Closes #48

Adds granular WordPress capability checks so each AI Agent ability (tool) can be granted independently to user roles, rather than all abilities being gated by a single hardcoded capability.

## Changes

### New: `ToolCapabilities` helper class (`includes/Abilities/ToolCapabilities.php`)

- **`cap_name(string $ability_id): string`** — derives `ai_agent_tool_{name}` from an ability ID (e.g. `ai-agent/memory-save` → `ai_agent_tool_memory_save`)
- **`current_user_can(string $ability_id): bool`** — checks the per-tool capability; falls back to `manage_options` if the capability hasn't been granted to any role yet (preserves existing admin-only default)
- **`capability_exists(string $cap): bool`** — checks whether a capability has been assigned to at least one role
- **`register_capabilities(array $ability_ids): void`** — adds all tool capabilities to the Administrator role so role-management plugins (Members, User Role Editor) can discover and assign them
- **`all_ability_ids(): array`** — canonical list of all 46 AI Agent ability IDs

### Filter: \`ai_agent_tool_capability\`

Allows overriding the resolved capability name per tool:

\`\`\`php
add_filter( 'ai_agent_tool_capability', function( string \$cap, string \$ability_id ): string {
    if ( \$ability_id === 'ai-agent/run-php' ) {
        return 'manage_network'; // Restrict to super admins on multisite.
    }
    return \$cap;
}, 10, 2 );
\`\`\`

### Updated: All 13 Abilities classes + CustomToolExecutor

Every `permission_callback` now delegates to `ToolCapabilities::current_user_can()` instead of hardcoded capability checks.

### Updated: `ai-agent.php`

Calls `ToolCapabilities::register_capabilities()` on plugin activation and `admin_init`.

### New: `tests/AiAgent/Abilities/ToolCapabilitiesTest.php`

8 test cases covering cap derivation, fallback logic, filter override, and registration.

## Behaviour

| Scenario | Result |
|---|---|
| Capability not granted to any role | Falls back to `manage_options` (admin only — unchanged) |
| Admin grants `ai_agent_tool_memory_save` to Editor role | Editors can use the memory-save tool |
| Filter overrides capability for `ai-agent/run-php` | Custom capability used instead |
| Plugin activated | All tool capabilities registered on Administrator role |

## Quality Gates

- ✅ PHPStan level 5: no errors
- ✅ PHPCS: no errors
- ✅ ESLint: no new errors (601 pre-existing prettier issues on `main`)
- ✅ Stylelint: no new errors (76 pre-existing issues on `main`)

title: t054: Add streaming response support via SSE
body:
## Summary

- Adds `POST /ai-agent/v1/stream` REST endpoint that emits `text/event-stream` responses, streaming AI tokens token-by-token to the browser
- Adds `SseStreamer` PHP helper class (`includes/REST/SseStreamer.php`) for SSE header management and event emission
- Updates `AgentLoop` to accept an `sse_streamer` option; when set, uses `send_prompt_direct_streaming()` via PHP `fopen` stream context to read the OpenAI-compatible SSE stream line-by-line and forward tokens in real time
- Emits `tool_call` and `tool_result` SSE events during agentic loops so the frontend can show tool activity as it happens
- Persists `awaiting_confirmation` state as a job transient so the existing `/job/{id}/confirm|reject` endpoints work with streamed sessions
- Adds `streamMessage` thunk in the Redux store using the Fetch API + `ReadableStream` to consume the SSE stream
- Adds streaming state (`streamingText`, `isStreaming`, `streamAbortController`) to the Redux store
- Updates `MessageList` to render a live streaming bubble with a blinking cursor while tokens arrive
- Updates `MessageInput` to use `streamMessage` when `fetch` + `ReadableStream` are available (falls back to `sendMessage` + polling for older browsers)
- Adds streaming cursor CSS animation to admin and floating-widget stylesheets

## SSE Event Protocol

| Event | Payload |
|-------|---------|
| `token` | `{"token": "..."}` — text delta |
| `tool_call` | `{"name": "...", "args": {...}}` |
| `tool_result` | `{"name": "...", "result": ...}` |
| `confirmation_required` | `{"job_id": "...", "pending_tools": [...]}` |
| `done` | `{"session_id": N, "token_usage": {...}, "model_id": "...", "cost_estimate": 0.0, "tool_calls": [...]}` |
| `error` | `{"code": "...", "message": "..."}` |

title: t089: MCP server — expose abilities as MCP tools for external AI clients
body:
## Summary

Implements the [Model Context Protocol (MCP)](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/) over a single WordPress REST endpoint, allowing external AI clients (Claude Desktop, Cursor, Continue, etc.) to discover and invoke all registered WordPress abilities as MCP tools.

## Changes

- **New**: `includes/REST/McpController.php` — MCP protocol handler
- **Modified**: `includes/REST/RestController.php` — registers the `/mcp` route on boot

## Endpoint

```
POST /wp-json/ai-agent/v1/mcp
```

### Authentication

WordPress nonce (`X-WP-Nonce` header) or Application Password (HTTP Basic Auth). Requires `manage_options` capability.

### Methods

#### `list_tools`

Returns all abilities registered via `wp_register_ability()` as MCP tool definitions:

```json
{
  "method": "list_tools"
}
```

Response:
```json
{
  "protocol_version": "2024-11-05",
  "tools": [
    {
      "name": "ai-agent__memory-save",
      "description": "Save a piece of information to persistent memory...",
      "inputSchema": { "type": "object", "properties": { ... } }
    }
  ]
}
```

#### `call_tool`

Executes a named ability with provided arguments:

```json
{
  "method": "call_tool",
  "params": {
    "name": "ai-agent__memory-save",
    "arguments": { "category": "general", "content": "User prefers dark mode" }
  }
}
```

Response:
```json
{
  "protocol_version": "2024-11-05",
  "tool": "ai-agent__memory-save",
  "isError": false,
  "content": [{ "type": "text", "text": "{\"saved\":true,\"id\":42}" }]
}
```

### Name mapping

Ability names use `namespace/tool-name` format (slash + hyphens). MCP tool names must match `[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+`, so the slash is replaced with `__`:

- `ai-agent/memory-save` → `ai-agent__memory-save`
- `ai-agent/discovery-list` → `ai-agent__discovery-list`

## Quality

- PHPCS: 0 errors, 0 warnings (auto-fixed 2 alignment warnings via phpcbf)
- PHPStan: No errors
- `npm run build`: compiled successfully

Closes #160

title: t006: Fix npm audit vulnerabilities (26 issues: 12 moderate, 14 high)
body:
## Summary

- Bumps `@wordpress/scripts` from `^31.2.0` to `^31.6.0` to pick up upstream security fixes
- Adds targeted `overrides` in `package.json` to force patched versions of transitive dependencies: `ajv`, `minimatch`, `flatted`, `immutable`, `serialize-javascript`, `svgo`, `webpack-dev-server`, `yauzl`
- Reduces vulnerability count from 26 (12 moderate, 14 high) to **0**

```
npm audit
# found 0 vulnerabilities

npm run build
# webpack 5.x compiled with 3 warnings (bundle-size only, pre-existing)

npx eslint src/ --ext .js,.jsx
# 0 errors, 1 pre-existing warning (@wordpress/no-unsafe-wp-apis)
```

## Approach

Direct dependency upgrades were not possible for all packages (transitive deps locked by `@wordpress/scripts`). The `overrides` field forces patched versions of vulnerable transitive packages without breaking the build or ESLint toolchain. Overrides are scoped where needed (e.g., `ajv` scoped to `@wp-playground/*` packages only) to avoid breaking tools that depend on specific versions.

title: t019: Add PHPUnit coverage reporting with pcov and Codecov
body:
## Summary

- Adds a new `coverage` CI job to `tests.yml` that installs pcov into the wp-env tests container, runs PHPUnit with `--coverage-clover`, and uploads `coverage.xml` to Codecov via `codecov/codecov-action@v5`
- Keeps the existing `phpunit` job unchanged (`coverage: none`) so fast test runs are not slowed by instrumentation overhead
- Adds `codecov.yml` with project/patch status checks, `phpunit` flag scoped to `includes/`, and ignore paths for `vendor/`, `node_modules/`, `build/`, `src/`, `tests/`
- Adds `wp-env:install-pcov` npm script and `test:php:coverage:ci` npm script for local and CI coverage runs

## Why pcov over xdebug

pcov is a dedicated coverage driver — 3-5x faster than xdebug, no debugging overhead. The wp-env tests container doesn't ship with either, so we install pcov at runtime via `pecl install pcov && docker-php-ext-enable pcov`. PHP headers are present in the container so the build succeeds.

## Why a separate job

Coverage instrumentation adds significant overhead to every function call. Keeping it in a separate job means the fast `phpunit` job (used for pass/fail gating) stays quick, while coverage runs in parallel without blocking the feedback loop.

## Setup required

To activate Codecov reporting, connect the repo at https://codecov.io and add a `CODECOV_TOKEN` secret to the repository (Settings → Secrets → Actions). The `fail_ci_if_error: false` setting means CI passes even if Codecov is not yet configured.

Closes #221

title: fix: replace wp-env Docker with direct MariaDB for PHPUnit CI
body:
## Summary

- Fixes the `PHPUnit (wp-env)` CI job that has never successfully run since wp-env was introduced in PR #88
- Root cause: `wp core multisite-install` fails inside the `wordpress:cli-php8.2` Docker container with an empty `Error:` message — the PHP 8.2 deprecation notice (trim() null) is a red herring; the real failure is multisite-install itself
- Fix: replace wp-env/Docker entirely with the standard WordPress plugin CI pattern (MariaDB service + `install-wp-tests.sh` + `vendor/bin/phpunit` directly on the runner)

## How it works

The new CI job:
1. Spins up a `mariadb:lts` service container
2. Runs `bin/install-wp-tests.sh` to download the WordPress test library to `/tmp/wordpress-tests-lib`
3. Runs `vendor/bin/phpunit` directly on the runner — no Docker, no wp-env, no WP-CLI

The `tests/bootstrap.php` already handles the `/tmp/wordpress-tests-lib` fallback path (it checks `/wordpress-phpunit` first for wp-env, then falls back to `sys_get_temp_dir()/wordpress-tests-lib`), so no bootstrap changes are needed.

## Why not the WP_CLI_PHP_ARGS approach (previous PR description)

The previous description was wrong. `WP_CLI_PHP_ARGS` set on the GitHub Actions host runner is never forwarded into the Docker container where WP-CLI runs. Even if it were, the actual failure is `wp core multisite-install` returning an empty error — not the deprecation notice. The deprecation notice is a red herring.

## Why not fix multisite-install inside Docker

The `.wp-env.json` has `MULTISITE: true` which triggers `wp core multisite-install` instead of `wp core install`. Multisite install is significantly more complex and fragile inside Docker. The tests themselves do not require multisite to run — `phpunit.xml.dist` sets `WP_TESTS_MULTISITE=1` as a constant, which is handled by the WordPress test library independently of how WordPress was installed.

## Trade-offs

- **Removed**: `npm ci`, `wp-env start`, `wp-env stop` steps (saves ~2-3 minutes per CI run)
- **Added**: `apt-get install subversion` (required by `install-wp-tests.sh` to download the test suite via SVN)
- **Unchanged**: `phpunit.xml.dist`, `tests/bootstrap.php`, `.wp-env.json` (wp-env still works for local development)

Closes #265

title: t054: Add streaming response support via SSE (Server-Sent Events)
body:
## Summary

- Adds `SseStreamer` class (`includes/REST/SseStreamer.php`) — low-level SSE plumbing: headers, output buffer flushing, typed event emitters (`token`, `tool_call`, `tool_result`, `confirmation_required`, `done`, `error`)
- Adds `POST /ai-agent/v1/stream` REST endpoint in `RestController` — runs the agent loop synchronously and streams tokens in real-time; handles tool confirmation pause by persisting state as a job transient and emitting `confirmation_required`
- Extends `AgentLoop` with optional `SseStreamer` injection; the OpenAI-compatible path uses `fopen`/`fgets` to read the upstream SSE stream and re-emits each text delta token immediately; tool call/result events are also streamed
- JS store (`src/store/index.js`): new `streamMessage` thunk uses Fetch API + `ReadableStream` to consume the SSE stream token-by-token; `appendStreamingText` / `setIsStreaming` actions manage the in-progress buffer; `stopGeneration` aborts via `AbortController`
- `MessageList` renders a live streaming bubble with a blinking cursor while `isStreaming` is true; committed as a proper message on `done`
- `MessageInput` auto-selects streaming when `window.ReadableStream` is available, falls back to polling (`sendMessage`) otherwise
- Debug panel and token usage stats work correctly in streaming mode via `done` event metadata

## Testing

1. Send a message in the chat — response should stream token-by-token instead of appearing all at once
2. Click Stop during streaming — generation aborts cleanly
3. Tool calls during streaming — `tool_call` / `tool_result` events appear in the debug panel; `confirmation_required` shows the confirmation dialog
4. Browsers without `ReadableStream` (old IE) — falls back to polling automatically
5. Session persistence — messages saved correctly after streaming completes

title: t029: Standardize error handling — return WP_Error not arrays with 'error' key
body:
## Summary

- Replaces all `return ['error' => '...']` patterns in ability handlers and tool executors with `new WP_Error(...)` objects
- Updates return type hints from `array` to `array|\WP_Error` on all affected handler methods
- Adds `/* translators: */` comments for all `sprintf(__())` calls with placeholders (PHPCS compliance)
- Fixes text domain from `'ai-agent'` to `'gratis-ai-agent'` in all new WP_Error strings (post-rename alignment)

## Why

The WordPress Abilities API resolver already converts `WP_Error` returns to `['error' => ...]` for the AI model, so this change is transparent to the model. Returning `WP_Error` is the idiomatic WordPress pattern per the project's own AGENTS.md rule: _"Return `WP_Error` objects; never throw exceptions in hooks"_.

This is a resubmission of PR #90, rebased onto main after the plugin rename (PR #194) was merged.

title: t074: Action cards for confirmable operations
body:
## Summary

- Adds an inline `ActionCard` component that renders directly in the message list when the agent proposes a tool call requiring user confirmation (permission set to `confirm`)
- Wires the Redux store (`pendingActionCard` state, `setPendingActionCard` action, `getPendingActionCard` selector) and `confirmToolCall`/`rejectToolCall` thunks to drive the card lifecycle
- Adds YOLO mode toggle to the General settings tab (skip all confirmations)

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/components/action-card.js` | New component — renders tool name, human-readable description, expandable args, Confirm/Cancel buttons with auto-focus |
| `src/store/index.js` | `pendingActionCard` state + action + selector; `pollJob` sets card on `awaiting_confirmation`; confirm/reject thunks clear it |
| `src/components/message-list.js` | Renders `ActionCard` inline; suppresses Thinking spinner while card is visible |
| `src/admin-page/style.css` | Action card styles (`.ai-agent-action-card-*`) |
| `src/floating-widget/style.css` | Compact action card styles for floating widget |
| `includes/Core/AgentLoop.php` | `get_tools_needing_confirmation()` returns tool details for the card; `run()` returns `awaiting_confirmation` + `pending_tools` |
| `includes/Core/Settings.php` | `yolo_mode` default in `get_defaults()` |
| `src/settings-page/settings-app.js` | YOLO mode toggle in General tab |

## How it works

1. User sends a message; agent loop runs and encounters a tool with permission `confirm`
2. Backend returns `status: awaiting_confirmation` with `pending_tools` array
3. Frontend `pollJob` sets `pendingActionCard` in the store
4. `MessageList` renders `ActionCard` inline below the last message; Thinking spinner is hidden
5. User clicks **Confirm** → `confirmToolCall` POST → job resumes; or **Cancel** → `rejectToolCall` POST → job resumes with rejection
6. Card clears from state on either action

Closes #212

title: t041: Update compat layer to match WordPress/ai Abstract_Ability pattern
body:
## Summary

- Adds `GratisAiAgent_Abstract_Ability` to the compat layer (`compat/abilities-api/class-abstract-ability.php`), mirroring the `WordPress\AI\Abstracts\Abstract_Ability` pattern from the [WordPress/ai plugin](https://github.com/WordPress/ai)
- Adds `GratisAiAgent\Abilities\AbstractAbility` (`includes/Abilities/AbstractAbility.php`) as a namespace-aware wrapper with sensible defaults for `category()` and `meta()`
- Updates `compat/load.php` to load the abstract class unconditionally after `WP_Ability` is available (whether from core or compat), ensuring it works on WP 6.9+
- Refactors all 13 Abilities factory classes to register via `ability_class` pointing to concrete `AbstractAbility` subclasses, replacing closures and static callbacks

## Why

The `WordPress/ai` plugin (the upstream reference implementation) uses an OOP pattern where each ability is a self-contained class extending `Abstract_Ability`. Our plugin was using a flat factory pattern with closures. This change aligns our implementation with the upstream pattern so that:

1. Migration to WordPress core `Abstract_Ability` (when it ships) requires minimal changes
2. Each ability is a typed, testable class with explicit schema and permission methods
3. The compat layer provides the abstract class on WP < 7.0 so the pattern works today

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `compat/abilities-api/class-abstract-ability.php` | New — global abstract class extending `WP_Ability` |
| `includes/Abilities/AbstractAbility.php` | New — namespaced wrapper with plugin defaults |
| `compat/load.php` | Updated — load abstract class unconditionally |
| `includes/Abilities/*.php` (13 files) | Refactored — registration uses `ability_class`, handlers moved to concrete subclasses |

## Verification

- `php -l` passes on all 16 modified/new files
- `npm run build` succeeds (3 warnings, all pre-existing)
- `composer dump-autoload` succeeds
- PHPCBF passes with zero remaining violations

Closes #233

title: t041: Update compat layer to match WordPress/ai Abstract_Ability pattern
body:
## Summary

- Adds `GratisAiAgent_Abstract_Ability` to the compat layer (`compat/abilities-api/class-abstract-ability.php`), mirroring the `WordPress\AI\Abstracts\Abstract_Ability` pattern from the [WordPress/ai plugin](https://github.com/WordPress/ai)
- Adds `GratisAiAgent\Abilities\AbstractAbility` (`includes/Abilities/AbstractAbility.php`) as a namespace-aware wrapper with sensible defaults for `category()` and `meta()`
- Updates `compat/load.php` to load the abstract class unconditionally after `WP_Ability` is available (whether from core or compat), ensuring it works on WP 6.9+
- Refactors all 13 Abilities factory classes to register via `ability_class` pointing to concrete `AbstractAbility` subclasses, replacing closures and static callbacks

## Why

The `WordPress/ai` plugin (the upstream reference implementation) uses an OOP pattern where each ability is a self-contained class extending `Abstract_Ability`. Our plugin was using a flat factory pattern with closures. This change aligns our implementation with the upstream pattern so that:

1. Migration to WordPress core `Abstract_Ability` (when it ships) requires minimal changes
2. Each ability is a typed, testable class with explicit schema and permission methods
3. The compat layer provides the abstract class on WP < 7.0 so the pattern works today

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `compat/abilities-api/class-abstract-ability.php` | New — global abstract class extending `WP_Ability` |
| `includes/Abilities/AbstractAbility.php` | New — namespaced wrapper with plugin defaults |
| `compat/load.php` | Updated — load abstract class unconditionally |
| `includes/Abilities/*.php` (13 files) | Refactored — registration uses `ability_class`, handlers moved to concrete subclasses |

## Verification

- `php -l` passes on all 16 modified/new files
- `npm run build` succeeds (3 warnings, all pre-existing)
- `composer dump-autoload` succeeds
- PHPCBF passes with zero remaining violations

Closes #233

title: t083: Push-to-talk speech-to-text via browser Web Speech API
body:
## Summary

- Adds a `useSpeechRecognition` hook (`src/components/use-speech-recognition.js`) that wraps the browser Web Speech API with clean start/stop/toggle controls, interim-results support, and a graceful no-op when the API is unavailable.
- Integrates a mic button into `MessageInput`: recognised speech is appended to the textarea; the button is hidden when the browser lacks `SpeechRecognition` or while a message is being sent.
- Mic button pulses red while recording with an accessible `aria-label`; returns to neutral when idle.
- CSS added to both `admin-page` and `floating-widget` entry points; textarea right-padding widened to accommodate the extra button.

## How it works

1. User clicks the mic button (or holds it for push-to-talk style).
2. Browser prompts for microphone permission on first use.
3. Recognised speech is appended to the textarea as interim results arrive.
4. User clicks again (or speech ends) to stop; text is ready to edit/send.
5. On browsers without `window.SpeechRecognition` / `window.webkitSpeechRecognition` the button is not rendered — no degradation.

## Testing

- Chrome/Edge (full support): mic button visible, click to start/stop, speech appended to textarea.
- Firefox (no Web Speech API): mic button not rendered, input area unchanged.
- Safari 14.1+: works via `webkitSpeechRecognition`.

Closes #393

title: t081: Proactive alerts — notification badge on FAB
body:
## Summary

- Adds a `GET /gratis-ai-agent/v1/alerts` REST endpoint that detects actionable issues (currently: no AI provider configured) and returns `{ count, alerts[] }`
- Adds `alertCount` state, `fetchAlerts` thunk, `setAlertCount` action, and `getAlertCount` selector to the Redux store
- `FloatingWidget` fetches alerts on mount and polls every 5 minutes
- `FloatingButton` renders a red notification badge (capped at `9+`) when `alertCount > 0`
- Fixes a pre-existing CSS class mismatch: `.ai-agent-fab` → `.gratis-ai-agent-fab` to match the `className` prop already used in `FloatingButton`

## How it works

The badge is a `<span>` absolutely positioned at the top-right of the FAB. It is only rendered when `alertCount > 0`, so there is zero visual change for fully-configured sites. The alert check is lightweight (reads a single WordPress option) and non-blocking (errors are silently swallowed, badge stays at 0).

## Extensibility

The `/alerts` endpoint is designed to accumulate checks over time — future alerts (e.g. expiring API key, failed automation, context window near limit) can be added by appending to the `$alerts` array in `handle_alerts()` without touching the frontend.

Closes #391

title: t080: Daily site health automation — SiteHealthAbilities
body:
## Summary

Implements t080: daily site health automation with six new WordPress Abilities and a dedicated tool profile.

## New Abilities

| Ability | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| `gratis-ai-agent/check-plugin-updates` | Lists plugins with available updates (uses cached transient, optional force refresh) |
| `gratis-ai-agent/scan-php-error-log` | Reads WP debug log with streaming (512 KB tail), filters by level and time window |
| `gratis-ai-agent/check-disk-space` | Reports total/free/used disk space, wp-content and uploads directory sizes |
| `gratis-ai-agent/check-security` | Checks 7 security indicators: debug mode, file editor, WP core version, admin username, inactive plugins, SSL, wp-config.php location |
| `gratis-ai-agent/check-performance` | Reports autoloaded options size, expired transients, post revision count, object cache status |
| `gratis-ai-agent/site-health-summary` | Runs all five checks in one call; returns `overall_status`: `healthy` / `needs_attention` / `critical` |

## Supporting Changes

- **`site-health` tool profile** — built-in profile scoped to the six new abilities (+ memory/skill/list-tools/execute-tool)
- **`Daily Site Health Report` automation template** — updated prompt uses `site-health-summary` and references the `site-health` tool profile; produces a structured report with critical issues, warnings, and passing checks

## Design Notes

- Log scanning uses `fopen`/`fseek` streaming (not `WP_Filesystem`) to avoid loading large log files into memory — phpcs:ignore comments explain the rationale
- Security score: starts at 100, deducts 20 per critical issue, 5 per warning
- All abilities are read-only (`readonly: true`, `idempotent: true` annotations)
- All abilities require `manage_options` (or `update_plugins` for the update check)

## Testing

1. Enable `WP_DEBUG_LOG` in wp-config.php and trigger a PHP notice
2. Use the AI chat with the `site-health` tool profile selected
3. Ask: "Run a site health check" — the agent should call `site-health-summary` and return a structured report

## Summary

- Wires `ChartBlock` into `MarkdownMessage` — AI responses can now include charts using standard markdown fences
- Graceful fallback: invalid JSON or missing `type`/`data` fields show an inline error + syntax-highlighted code block

## Usage

The AI can now produce charts in responses using:

````
```chart
{
  "type": "bar",
  "data": {
    "labels": ["Jan", "Feb", "Mar"],
    "datasets": [{ "label": "Revenue", "data": [120, 190, 300] }]
  }
}
```
````

title: t033: Port GitTracker class — store original files as git blobs, track changes
body:
## Summary

- Implements `Models/GitTracker` — per-package (plugin/theme) tracker that stores original file content as binary blobs in the database before AI modifications, with `snapshotFile()`, `revertFile()`, `getDiff()`, `getTrackedFiles()`, `getModifiedFiles()`, and `clearTracking()` methods.
- Implements `Models/GitTrackerManager` — registry/factory for `GitTracker` instances; hooks into `gratis_ai_agent_before/after_file_write/edit` actions to auto-snapshot files transparently before any `FileAbilities` write or edit operation.
- Implements `Abilities/GitAbilities` — six WordPress Abilities exposing git tracking to the AI agent:
  - `gratis-ai-agent/git-snapshot` — explicitly snapshot a file
  - `gratis-ai-agent/git-diff` — unified diff between original and current
  - `gratis-ai-agent/git-restore` — restore a single file to its original
  - `gratis-ai-agent/git-list` — list all tracked files with status
  - `gratis-ai-agent/git-package-summary` — summary for a plugin/theme package
  - `gratis-ai-agent/git-revert-package` — revert all modified files in a package
- Updates `FileAbilities` to fire `gratis_ai_agent_before/after_file_write/edit` hooks (auto-snapshot integration).
- Adds `git_tracked_files` DB table schema and bumps `DB_VERSION` to `10.0.0`.
- Registers `GitAbilities` and `GitTrackerManager` in the main plugin file.

## Design notes

- No git binary required — all storage is in the WordPress database (`longblob` column).
- Original content is immutable once stored; re-snapshot requires `clearTracking()` first.
- Diff uses WordPress's `wp_text_diff()` when available, with a pure-PHP LCS fallback.
- `GitTrackerManager::forFile()` auto-resolves plugin vs theme from the file path.
- PHPCS: zero violations. PHP syntax: clean. PHPStan: 9 pre-existing errors unchanged.

Closes #431

title: t070: WooCommerce abilities — product CRUD, order queries, store stats
body:
## Summary

Implements issue #424: adds a `WooCommerceAbilities` class with six WordPress Abilities API tools for interacting with WooCommerce stores.

## Abilities added

| Ability slug | Description |
|---|---|
| `woo-get-products` | List/search/fetch products — filter by status, category, stock status, search term, or single ID |
| `woo-create-product` | Create simple, variable, grouped, or external products |
| `woo-update-product` | Partial update of any product field (only provided fields are changed) |
| `woo-delete-product` | Move to trash or force-delete a product |
| `woo-get-orders` | Query orders by status, customer ID/email, date range, or product ID |
| `woo-get-store-stats` | Revenue (total/net/tax/shipping), order counts by status, top-selling products, unique customer counts |

## Design decisions

- **WooCommerce PHP API only** — uses `wc_get_product()`, `wc_get_orders()`, `WC_Product_*` classes directly. No WooCommerce REST API HTTP calls needed; runs in-process with full WC context.
- **Conditional registration** — abilities only register when `class_exists('WooCommerce')` is true. Safe to ship in the plugin without WooCommerce as a hard dependency.
- **Permission model** — read abilities (`get-products`, `get-orders`, `get-store-stats`) require `view_woocommerce_reports` or `manage_woocommerce`; write abilities require `manage_woocommerce`.
- **Pagination** — product and order queries support `per_page`/`page` with `paginate: true` to return total counts.
- **phpcs.xml** — adds `manage_woocommerce` and `view_woocommerce_reports` as known custom capabilities so PHPCS does not flag them.

## Verification

- `php -l` passes on both modified files
- `vendor/bin/phpcs --standard=phpcs.xml includes/Abilities/WooCommerceAbilities.php` — zero violations
- `npm run build` — compiles with 0 errors (pre-existing bundle size warnings only)

title: t063: Smart onboarding — agent scans existing site on first activation
body:
## Summary

- Adds `SiteScanner`: a WP-Cron background job (fires 10s after activation) that collects plugins, active theme, post types, post count, categories, WooCommerce status, and site identity — then stores results as `site_info` / `technical_notes` memories and seeds the knowledge base with the first 50 published posts.
- Adds `OnboardingManager`: orchestrates the trigger (activation hook + `admin_init` fallback for upgrades), exposes `GET /gratis-ai-agent/v1/onboarding/status` and `POST /gratis-ai-agent/v1/onboarding/rescan` REST endpoints.
- Wires both classes into `gratis-ai-agent.php` (activation/deactivation hooks + bootstrap registration).

## What changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `includes/Core/SiteScanner.php` | New — background scan + memory storage + knowledge seeding |
| `includes/Core/OnboardingManager.php` | New — trigger orchestration + REST endpoints |
| `gratis-ai-agent.php` | Modified — activation hook, deactivation cleanup, bootstrap call |
| `todo/tasks/t063-brief.md` | New — task brief |

## Behaviour

1. **Fresh install**: activation hook fires → `OnboardingManager::on_activation()` → schedules `gratis_ai_agent_site_scan` cron event (10s delay).
2. **Upgrade from pre-onboarding version**: `admin_init` fires → `maybe_trigger()` detects no memories and no prior scan → schedules scan.
3. **Subsequent activations**: `TRIGGERED_OPTION` is set → no re-scan.
4. **Manual rescan**: `POST /gratis-ai-agent/v1/onboarding/rescan` resets state and re-schedules.

## Site type detection

Heuristic order: WooCommerce active → LMS plugins → Membership plugins → Portfolio/Elementor → post count > 20 → brochure.

## Blocks

Unblocks t064 (onboarding interview) and t071 (WooCommerce onboarding).

Closes #417

  - `setSiteBuilderMode(enabled)` action
  - `SET_SITE_BUILDER_MODE` reducer case
  - `isSiteBuilderMode(state)` and `isFreshInstall(state)` selectors

- **`src/floating-widget/index.js`**
  - Reads `siteBuilderMode` from store
  - `useEffect` auto-calls `setFloatingOpen(true)` when `siteBuilderMode` is active, so the panel opens immediately on first admin page load without requiring a FAB click

## Detection logic

A site is considered a fresh install when **all** of the following are true:

1. No published posts exist beyond the default "Hello world!" sample
2. No published pages exist beyond the default "Sample Page" / "Privacy Policy"
3. The active theme is one of the built-in WordPress Twenty* themes

Once the user publishes real content or switches to a custom theme, `site_builder_mode` remains set (it's a flag, not re-evaluated on every load) — the site builder flow can check this flag to know whether to show setup prompts.

## Testing

1. Fresh WordPress install with default theme → floating widget opens automatically on any admin page
2. Publish a post → `FreshInstallDetector::isFreshInstall()` returns `false` after transient expires (≤5 min)
3. Switch to a custom theme → same
4. `GET /wp-json/gratis-ai-agent/v1/fresh-install` returns correct status object

Closes #414

title: t061: Site builder conversation flow — interview user then generate full site
body:
## Summary

Implements t061: a guided site builder conversation flow that interviews the user about their business and then autonomously generates a complete WordPress site.

Closes #415

## What's included

### New: `SiteBuilderAbilities` (4 tools)
- `gratis-ai-agent/detect-fresh-install` — checks post count, page count, nav menus to determine if the site is a fresh install
- `gratis-ai-agent/set-site-builder-mode` — enables/disables site builder mode (stored in settings)
- `gratis-ai-agent/get-site-builder-status` — returns current mode state + site info
- `gratis-ai-agent/complete-site-builder` — marks onboarding done, disables site builder mode

### Site builder system prompt (`AgentLoop::get_site_builder_system_prompt()`)
Three-phase workflow:
1. **Interview** — asks one question at a time: business name, type, audience, goals, pages, tone, content
2. **Build** — autonomously executes: site title/tagline, all pages with real content, static homepage, nav menu, hero image, memory save, complete-site-builder call
3. **Summary** — lists created pages with URLs and next steps

### Settings
- Added `site_builder_mode` (bool, default `false`) to `Settings::get_defaults()`
- `AgentLoop::build_system_instruction()` uses the site builder prompt when `site_builder_mode` is active, bypassing the default/custom prompt

### REST API
- `POST /gratis-ai-agent/v1/site-builder/start` — enables mode, creates a dedicated session, returns session ID + system prompt
- `GET /gratis-ai-agent/v1/site-builder/status` — returns mode state + fresh install detection
- `GET /gratis-ai-agent/v1/alerts` — extended to include `site_builder_mode` and `onboarding_complete` flags; adds a `site_builder_mode` alert when active

### Frontend
- `FloatingWidget::enqueue_assets()` passes `siteBuilderMode`, `onboardingComplete`, REST endpoints, and nonce to JS via `wp_localize_script` as `window.gratisAiAgentSiteBuilder`
- `floating-widget/index.js` — when `siteBuilderMode` is true: auto-opens the panel and injects the opening interview greeting as an assistant message so the user sees the first question immediately

## Blocked by
t060 (detect fresh install + trigger site builder mode) is still open. This PR implements the conversation flow and all the tooling. t060 will wire up the automatic trigger on fresh installs; this PR provides the `set-site-builder-mode` ability and REST endpoint that t060 will call.

## Testing
1. Enable site builder mode via REST: `POST /gratis-ai-agent/v1/site-builder/start`
2. Reload any admin page — the floating widget should auto-open with the greeting
3. Answer the interview questions; after the last answer the agent should build the full site autonomously
4. Verify `gratis-ai-agent/complete-site-builder` is called at the end (disables mode, sets `onboarding_complete`)

title: t053: CodeMirror 6 syntax highlighting for chat code blocks
body:
## Summary

Replaces `react-syntax-highlighter` (Prism) with **CodeMirror 6** for syntax-highlighted, read-only code display in chat responses.

## Changes

- **`src/components/code-block.js`** — Rewritten to use `@codemirror/view` `EditorView` in read-only mode. Destroy+recreate pattern on code/language change keeps the implementation simple and correct.
- **`src/admin-page/style.css`** — Updated comment; added `.ai-agent-code-cm` focus outline suppression.
- **`src/floating-widget/style.css`** — Added `.ai-agent-code-block` styles for the floating panel context (compact sizing).
- **`package.json`** — Removed `react-syntax-highlighter`; added 11 `@codemirror/*` packages.

## Features

| Feature | Implementation |
|---------|---------------|
| Syntax highlighting | CodeMirror 6 language extensions (tree-shaken) |
| Line numbers | `lineNumbers()` extension, always visible |
| Copy to clipboard | Button in header, 2s confirmation feedback |
| Theme | One Dark (`@codemirror/theme-one-dark`) |
| Read-only | `EditorView.editable.of(false)` + `EditorState.readOnly.of(true)` |
| Languages | PHP, JS/JSX/TS/TSX, HTML, CSS/SCSS, SQL, Python, JSON, YAML, Markdown, Rust |

## Lazy loading

CodeMirror only instantiates when a `CodeBlock` component renders. `CodeBlock` is only rendered by `MarkdownMessage` when a fenced code block is present in the AI response — so CodeMirror is effectively lazy: zero runtime cost when no code blocks are in the conversation.

## Bundle size

| Bundle | Before | After | Delta |
|--------|--------|-------|-------|
| admin-page.js | ~857 KB | ~1.13 MB | +274 KB |
| floating-widget.js | ~857 KB | ~1.07 MB | +213 KB |

The increase is the CodeMirror 6 core + language parsers. This replaces `react-syntax-highlighter` which was ~200 KB. CodeMirror 6 is more capable (line numbers, editor-grade highlighting) at a comparable size.

Closes #384

title: t086: Google Search Console SEO insights abilities
body:
## Summary

- Adds four WordPress AI agent abilities that query the Google Search Console API to surface SEO performance data directly in the AI chat interface
- Implements secure credential storage (service-account JSON key or OAuth2 access token) in a dedicated `wp_options` entry — credentials are never returned through `GET /settings`
- Adds two REST endpoints (`POST`/`DELETE /settings/gsc-credentials`) for credential management from the settings UI

## Abilities added

| Ability | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| `gratis-ai-agent/gsc-top-queries` | Top search queries with clicks, impressions, CTR, and average position. Supports page/country/device filters. |
| `gratis-ai-agent/gsc-page-performance` | Page-level performance data — which pages get the most impressions and clicks. |
| `gratis-ai-agent/gsc-query-details` | Deep-dive on a specific query: overall metrics + which pages rank for it. |
| `gratis-ai-agent/gsc-site-summary` | Site-wide totals with optional period-over-period comparison. |

## Authentication

Two modes supported:

1. **Service-account JSON key** — JWT signed with RSA-SHA256 via OpenSSL, exchanged for a short-lived access token cached in a WordPress transient (55-minute TTL).
2. **OAuth2 access token** — pre-obtained token, user-managed refresh.

## Security

- Credentials stored in `gratis_ai_agent_gsc_credentials` option (separate from general settings)
- `GET /settings` exposes only `{ configured: bool, type: string, default_site_url: string }` — no credential values
- All abilities require `manage_options` capability
- Specific 403/404 error messages guide users to fix GSC property access issues

## Files changed

- `includes/Abilities/GscAbilities.php` — new ability class (900+ lines)
- `includes/Core/Settings.php` — `get_gsc_credentials()`, `set_gsc_credentials()`, `has_gsc_credentials()`, `GSC_CREDENTIALS_OPTION` constant
- `includes/REST/RestController.php` — route registration + `handle_set_gsc_credentials()`, `handle_delete_gsc_credentials()`, GSC flag in `handle_get_settings()`
- `gratis-ai-agent.php` — `use` statement + `GscAbilities::register()` call

Closes #396

title: t084: Text-to-speech for AI responses (optional)
body:
## Summary

- Adds optional text-to-speech that reads AI responses aloud using the Web Speech API (`SpeechSynthesis`) — no external dependencies, fully client-side

- New **Text-to-Speech** settings tab with voice selector, rate, and pitch controls

## Changes

### New file
- `src/components/use-text-to-speech.js` — React hook wrapping `SpeechSynthesis` with markdown stripping, voice/rate/pitch config, and cleanup on unmount. Exports `useAvailableVoices` for async voice loading (Chrome fires `voiceschanged` after page load).

### Modified files
- **`src/store/index.js`** — Added `ttsEnabled`, `ttsVoiceURI`, `ttsRate`, `ttsPitch` state, actions (`setTtsEnabled`, `setTtsVoiceURI`, `setTtsRate`, `setTtsPitch`), and selectors. All four values are persisted to `localStorage` so the preference survives page reloads.

- **`src/components/message-list.js`** — `useEffect` watches for new model messages; calls `speak()` when TTS is enabled, streaming is complete, and the message hasn't been spoken yet. Cancels speech when TTS is disabled mid-conversation.
- **`src/settings-page/settings-app.js`** — New **Text-to-Speech** tab with: enable toggle, voice `<select>` (populated from `useAvailableVoices`), rate slider (0.5–2), pitch slider (0–2). Falls back gracefully when browser doesn't support TTS.
- **`src/admin-page/style.css`** / **`src/floating-widget/style.css`** — TTS button styles for both admin page and floating widget contexts.

## Behaviour

- TTS is **off by default** — opt-in only
- Toggle button in the chat header provides quick on/off without going to settings
- When enabled, each AI response is spoken once it finishes streaming
- Markdown is stripped before speaking (code blocks, headers, bold/italic, links, list markers)
- Voice, rate, and pitch are configurable in Settings → Text-to-Speech
- Speech is cancelled immediately when TTS is toggled off
- Gracefully no-ops in browsers without `SpeechSynthesis` support (the button is hidden)

title: t076: Resale API proxy endpoint with usage tracking
body:
## Summary

- Adds a managed AI resale layer so site owners can expose their configured AI provider to downstream clients under their own API keys
- Per-client monthly token quota enforcement with automatic monthly reset
- Full per-request usage logging (tokens, cost, model, duration, status) with paginated log and aggregated summary endpoints

## New endpoints

| Method | Path | Auth | Description |
|--------|------|------|-------------|
| `POST` | `/resale/proxy` | `X-Resale-API-Key` header | OpenAI-compatible proxy — forwards request to site's AI provider |
| `GET` | `/resale/clients` | admin | List all resale clients |
| `POST` | `/resale/clients` | admin | Create client (returns API key once) |
| `GET` | `/resale/clients/{id}` | admin | Get client details |
| `PATCH` | `/resale/clients/{id}` | admin | Update client |
| `DELETE` | `/resale/clients/{id}` | admin | Delete client + usage logs |
| `POST` | `/resale/clients/{id}/rotate-key` | admin | Rotate API key (returns new key once) |
| `GET` | `/resale/clients/{id}/usage` | admin | Paginated usage log |
| `GET` | `/resale/clients/{id}/usage/summary` | admin | Aggregated totals (filterable by date range) |

## New DB tables

- `{prefix}gratis_ai_agent_resale_clients` — client credentials, quota config, counters
- `{prefix}gratis_ai_agent_resale_usage` — per-request audit log

DB version bumped `10.0.0` → `11.0.0`.

## Implementation notes

- Proxy response is OpenAI-compatible (`chat.completion` object) so existing OpenAI SDK clients work without modification
- API keys are prefixed `gaa_` and never returned after creation/rotation
- Markup percent applies a cost multiplier for billing purposes (stored in usage log)
- `max_iterations: 1` on AgentLoop for proxy calls — single-turn only, no agentic loops
- Monthly quota auto-resets when `quota_reset_at` passes on the next request

title: fix: guard task completion against unmerged PRs
body:
## Summary

- Adds a project-level `task-complete-helper.sh` wrapper that checks `gh pr view --json state,mergedAt` and aborts if the PR is not merged before delegating to the aidevops framework script
- Adds a `todo-integrity` CI workflow that validates all completed tasks in `TODO.md` with `pr:#NNN` references have merged PRs
- Documents the rule in `.agents/AGENTS.md`

## Root Cause

A worker called `task-complete-helper.sh t085 --pr 465` immediately after opening PR #465, before it was merged. This caused `TODO.md` to show t085 as complete while the PR was still open.

## Fix

Three-layer defense:

1. **`.agents/scripts/task-complete-helper.sh`** — project-level wrapper that enforces the merge check before delegating to the framework script. Supports `--skip-merge-check` for tests and `--gh-repo` for cross-repo PRs.

2. **`.github/workflows/todo-integrity.yml`** — CI check that runs on every push/PR touching `TODO.md`. Fails with a clear error if any completed task references an unmerged PR.

3. **`.agents/AGENTS.md`** — documents the rule and root cause for future workers.

The aidevops framework fix is in [marcusquinn/aidevops PR #5066](https://github.com/marcusquinn/aidevops/pull/5066).

Closes #466

title: fix: redact secrets/PII in ChangeLogger before_value/after_value
body:
## Summary

- Adds `is_sensitive_option()` — keyword-pattern check (`api_key`, `token`, `secret`, `password`, `pass`, `auth`, `client`, `authorization`, `cookie`) to detect credential-like option names
- Adds `redact_value()` helper returning `[REDACTED]` constant

The change log still records *that* a sensitive option was modified (field name, session, ability) — it just no longer stores the raw value in plain text.

## Motivation

CodeRabbit review on PR #447 flagged that `ChangeLogger` was persisting raw option values into `ChangesLog::record`, which could leak API keys, tokens, passwords, and user email addresses stored in WordPress options.

## Testing

- Non-sensitive options (e.g., `blogname`, `siteurl`) continue to log before/after values unchanged
- Options matching sensitive patterns (e.g., `my_plugin_api_key`, `oauth_token`, `admin_password`) log `[REDACTED]` for both before and after values
- `user_email` profile changes log `[REDACTED]` for both values; `display_name` and `user_url` continue to log normally

title: fix: correct allSelected header checkbox logic for cross-page selections (#490)
body:
## Summary

Fixes the header checkbox in the Changes page that incorrectly showed as checked when navigating between pages, even though the current page rows were not selected.

## Root Cause

`allSelected` compared counts (`selectedIds.length === changes.length`) instead of membership. After selecting all rows on page 1 and navigating to page 2, both arrays had the same length — so the checkbox appeared checked even though page 2 rows were not selected.

`handleSelectAll` also replaced the entire selection with the current page's ids (or cleared everything), destroying cross-page selections.

## Changes

- **`allSelected`**: now uses `currentPageIds.every(id => selectedIds.includes(id))` — checks that every visible row on the current page is in the selection set
- **`handleSelectAll`**: now performs union (add current page ids) when checked, and difference (remove current page ids) when unchecked — preserving selections from other pages
- **`handleSelectOne`**: already used membership correctly, no change needed
- **Export**: uses `selectedIds` directly (unchanged) — correctly exports all selected ids across all pages

## Testing

- Select all on page 1, navigate to page 2 → header checkbox should be unchecked
- Select all on page 1, select all on page 2 → header checkbox checked on both pages
- Uncheck all on page 2 → page 1 selections preserved
- Export with cross-page selections → all selected ids exported

Closes #490

title: feat: improve multi-step agentic workflows and add model benchmark suite
body:
## Summary

- **Hide intermediate tools from AI models** — `markdown-to-blocks` and `create-block-content` are now hidden (`ai_hidden` meta) from the model's tool list. Models were calling these instead of `create-post`, producing converted blocks that never got saved. The abilities still exist for internal/programmatic use.
- **Auto-convert markdown to Gutenberg blocks** — `create-post` and `update-post` now detect markdown content (## headings, **bold**, - lists) and auto-convert to serialized Gutenberg blocks server-side. Models can write natural markdown instead of wrestling with block HTML.
- **Composite `create-post-with-image` ability** — creates a post AND imports a stock image as featured image in a single tool call, eliminating the most common multi-step failure pattern.
- **`featured_image_id` parameter** added to `create-post` and `update-post` so models can set featured images from `import-stock-image` results.
- **Tool result truncation** — new `ToolResultTruncator` class prevents context bloat in long workflows by truncating large tool results (plugin lists, DB queries, HTML) before adding to conversation history. Full results remain in the tool call log.
- **Improved system prompt** — dedicated "Content Creation" section, explicit instruction to call all needed tools in one response, mentions composite tools.
- **Cross-reference hints** — `import-stock-image` results now include a `tip` field pointing models to use `attachment_id` as `featured_image_id`.
- **Model benchmark suite** — `tests/benchmark/model-benchmark.mjs` tests 7 WP admin prompts against synthetic.new models with automated scoring.

## Benchmark Results

Tested against 6 models on synthetic.new (GLM-4.7, GLM-4.7-Flash, Kimi-K2.5, Kimi-K2.5-NVFP4, MiniMax-M2.5, Nemotron-3-Super-120B):

| Metric | Before | After |
|--------|--------|-------|
| Average score (all models) | 54% | **77%** |
| Multi-step post+image task | 46% | **80%+** |
| Worst model score | 32% | **72%** |

### Files Changed

|------|--------|
| `includes/Abilities/PostAbilities.php` | Improved descriptions, `featured_image_id`, markdown auto-convert, composite ability |
| `includes/Abilities/BlockAbilities.php` | `ai_hidden` meta on `markdown-to-blocks` and `create-block-content` |
| `includes/Core/AgentLoop.php` | `ai_hidden` filter, tool result truncation, improved system prompt |

title: fix: move $instance creation before /stream route to fix non-static permission callback
body:
## Summary

- Moves `$instance = new self()` from after the `/stream` route registration to before it
- Changes `permission_callback` on `/stream` from `[ __CLASS__, 'check_chat_permission' ]` to `[ $instance, 'check_chat_permission' ]`
- The `/run` route reuses the same `$instance` (no duplicate instantiation)

## Root cause

`check_chat_permission()` is a non-static instance method. Registering it via `__CLASS__` caused PHP to attempt a static call, producing:

```
Fatal error: Uncaught TypeError: call_user_func(): Argument #1 ($callback) must be a valid callback,
non-static method GratisAiAgent\REST\RestController::check_chat_permission() cannot be called statically
```

This crashed 100% of chat requests — the frontend showed "Thinking..." indefinitely.

## Fix

Two-line change: move `$instance = new self()` up 60 lines, change `__CLASS__` to `$instance` for the permission callback. `handle_stream` remains `[ __CLASS__, 'handle_stream' ]` since it is correctly declared `static`.

Closes #509

title: t096: Add proper error handling for chat stream failures
body:
## Summary

- Adds a 120-second timeout to `streamMessage` via `AbortController`; the timer resets on each received chunk so long-running streams are not prematurely cut off
- Detects non-SSE `Content-Type` responses (e.g. PHP fatal error HTML pages) before reading the stream body, showing a descriptive error instead of hanging indefinitely
- Verifies the response `Content-Type` is `text/event-stream` after a 200 OK — catches misconfigured servers that return JSON or HTML with a 200 status
- Adds `streamError` flag and `lastUserMessage` to the Redux store; sets the flag on any stream failure, clears it on success
- Adds `retryLastMessage` thunk: removes the error system message and the preceding user message, then resends via `streamMessage`
- Shows a **"Try again"** button in `MessageList` when `streamError` is set and the last visible message is a system error
- All new user-facing strings use `__()` for i18n

## Changes

body:
## Summary

- Removes the `wp_ai_client_prompt()` availability guard from `enqueue_assets_frontend()` in `FloatingWidget.php`

`enqueue_assets_frontend()` had an early-return guard:

title: fix: address critical quality-debt review feedback from PR #407
body:
## Summary

Addresses all actionable review findings from PR #407 (CodeRabbit review), tracked in issue #504.

## Security fixes

### CRITICAL: Multisite privilege escalation in `StockImageAbilities`
`permission_callback` was checking `current_user_can('upload_files')` against the current blog only. On multisite, a user with upload rights on site A but not site B could import media into site B by passing its URL. Fixed by adding `StockImageAbilities::check_permission()` which resolves the target blog from `site_url` and checks the capability while switched to that blog.

### CRITICAL: SSRF in `SeoAbilities::handle_audit_url()`
`wp_remote_get()` was used on a user-supplied URL. `esc_url_raw()` formats the URL but does not block private IP ranges or loopback addresses. Replaced with `wp_safe_remote_get()` and added an explicit `wp_http_validate_url()` guard.

### MAJOR: Host-substring attack in `NavigationAbilities` URL validation
`strpos($url, $home_url) === 0` accepts `https://example.com.evil.tld/` as a same-site URL. Replaced with a parsed scheme/host/port comparison using `wp_parse_url()`, with path-prefix check for subdirectory installs.

## Quality fixes

### MAJOR: `libxml` global state leak in `SeoAbilities::parse_seo_elements()`
`libxml_use_internal_errors(true)` was never restored. Wrapped in `try/finally` to restore the previous mode after parsing.

### MINOR: Missing `declare(strict_types=1)` in `AbilityDiscoveryAbilities`
Added per project coding guidelines.

### NITPICK: PSR-4 class/filename mismatch in `NavigationAbilities`
`NavigateAbility` and `GetPageHtmlAbility` were defined inline in `NavigationAbilities.php`. Extracted to `NavigateAbility.php` and `GetPageHtmlAbility.php` per the project rule that class names must match filenames. `NavigationAbilities.php` now only handles registration/proxy wiring.

## Files changed

- `includes/Abilities/StockImageAbilities.php` — multisite permission fix
- `includes/Abilities/SeoAbilities.php` — SSRF fix + libxml state fix
- `includes/Abilities/NavigationAbilities.php` — URL validation fix + class extraction
- `includes/Abilities/NavigateAbility.php` — new file (extracted from NavigationAbilities)
- `includes/Abilities/GetPageHtmlAbility.php` — new file (extracted from NavigationAbilities)
- `includes/Abilities/AbilityDiscoveryAbilities.php` — strict_types declaration

Closes #504

title: fix: handle WP_Error return from get_the_terms() in WooCommerceAbilities
body:
## Summary

Fixes a potential fatal error in `WooCommerceAbilities::serialize_product()` when `get_the_terms()` returns a `WP_Error` object.

## Problem

`get_the_terms()` can return three types:
- `false` — no terms found
- `WP_Term[]` — success
- `WP_Error` — taxonomy not registered or other error

The previous `?: []` fallback only handles falsy values. `WP_Error` is truthy, so `array_map()` would receive a `WP_Error` object and produce a fatal error.

## Fix

Extracted a private `get_term_array(int $post_id, string $taxonomy): array` helper that validates with `is_wp_error()` before returning the terms, falling back to `[]` on failure. Applied to both `product_cat` and `product_tag` mappings.

## Verification

- PHPCS: pass
- PHPStan: pass (no errors)

Closes #503

title: fix: pass wp-env override JSON via env var to avoid shell quote stripping (closes #536)
body:
## Summary

- Fixes Playwright E2E (WP trunk) CI failure caused by invalid JSON in the wp-env override script
- Root cause: `${{ matrix.wp_env_override }}` was interpolated directly into a `node -e "..."` shell string, stripping the double-quotes from the JSON keys
- Fix: pass the override value as an environment variable (`WP_ENV_OVERRIDE`) and read it via `process.env.WP_ENV_OVERRIDE` — env vars bypass shell quoting entirely

## Root Cause

In `.github/workflows/e2e.yml`, the step "Override wp-env core version" ran:

```js
const override = JSON.parse('${{ matrix.wp_env_override }}');
```

When GitHub Actions expanded `${{ matrix.wp_env_override }}` (value: `{"core":"WordPress/WordPress#master"}`), the shell interpreted the double-quotes inside the `node -e "..."` double-quoted string, stripping them. The Node script received `{core:WordPress/WordPress#master}` — invalid JSON — causing:

```
SyntaxError: Expected property name or '}' in JSON at position 1
```

## Fix

Pass the matrix value as an environment variable and read it via `process.env`:

```yaml
env:
  WP_ENV_OVERRIDE: ${{ matrix.wp_env_override }}
run: |
  node -e "
    const override = JSON.parse(process.env.WP_ENV_OVERRIDE);
    ...
  "
```

Environment variables are not subject to shell quote interpretation, so the JSON structure is preserved intact.

## Verification

- Locally confirmed: `WP_ENV_OVERRIDE='{"core":"WordPress/WordPress#master"}' node -e "JSON.parse(process.env.WP_ENV_OVERRIDE)"` parses successfully
- Locally confirmed: the old approach `JSON.parse('{core:WordPress/WordPress#master}')` throws `SyntaxError` as expected
- CI: Playwright E2E (WP trunk) check must pass green

Closes #536

title: fix: resolve PHPUnit (WP trunk) fatal — ClientWithOptionsInterface namespace mismatch (#535)
body:
## Summary

Fixes the PHP fatal error that has been failing PHPUnit (WP trunk) CI for 7+ consecutive runs.

## Root Cause

WP trunk's bundled `php-ai-client` scopes its PSR dependencies under `WordPress\AiClientDependencies\Psr\` (via a custom autoloader in `wp-includes/php-ai-client/autoload.php`). The Composer-installed `wordpress/php-ai-client` package uses the global `Psr\` namespace.

When both are present in the same PHP process, Composer's autoloader wins the race for `WordPress\AiClient\Providers\Http\Contracts\ClientWithOptionsInterface` and registers it with **global** `Psr\` type hints. WP trunk's adapter class (`class-wp-ai-client-http-client.php`) then fails to implement it because it uses `WordPress\AiClientDependencies\Psr\` type hints:

```
PHP Fatal error: Declaration of WP_AI_Client_HTTP_Client::sendRequestWithOptions(
  WordPress\AiClientDependencies\Psr\Http\Message\RequestInterface $request, ...)
must be compatible with
  ClientWithOptionsInterface::sendRequestWithOptions(
  Psr\Http\Message\RequestInterface $request, ...)
```

## Fix

Two files changed:

**`tests/bootstrap.php`** — registers a prepended `spl_autoload_register` handler (runs before Composer's autoloader) that intercepts `WordPress\AiClient\Providers\Http\Contracts\ClientWithOptionsInterface`. When WP trunk's scoped PSR namespace is detectable (`interface_exists('WordPress\AiClientDependencies\Psr\Http\Message\RequestInterface')`), it loads the shim instead of Composer's version.

**`tests/stubs/wp-trunk-client-with-options-interface.php`** — the shim: defines `ClientWithOptionsInterface` in the `WordPress\AiClient\Providers\Http\Contracts` namespace using `WordPress\AiClientDependencies\Psr\` type hints, matching WP trunk's interface exactly.

## Behaviour

- **WP trunk**: shim activated → interface uses `WordPress\AiClientDependencies\Psr\` → WP trunk's adapter class implements it correctly → no fatal
- **WP 6.9**: `WordPress\AiClientDependencies\Psr\Http\Message\RequestInterface` does not exist → shim skipped → Composer's version used → our compat layer implements it correctly → no change

## Verification

PHPUnit (WP trunk) CI check must pass green.

Closes #535
