title: t166: make client-abilities registration async-aware (verified in browser)
body:
## Summary

Closes the runtime gap left after #821 (t165). Browser smoke test in headless Chromium against \`http://wordpress.local:8080\` now confirms client-side abilities register, list, dispatch, and round-trip end-to-end.

For #806 — final fix in the #815 → #821 → #819 (the rate-limit-bypass review-gate issue) → t166 chain.

## What was still broken after #821

PR #821 wired the entry-point imports so \`src/abilities/index.js\` actually ran. That immediately surfaced **three more bugs** in the registry code (originally shipped in #815, hidden previously because the imports were never firing). A real browser session caught all three with explicit \`pageerror\` messages:

\`\`\`text
pageerror: Ability name is required
pageerror: The category properties must contain a \`description\` string.
pageerror: Ability "gratis-ai-agent-js/navigate-to" references non-existent category "gratis-ai-agent-js". Please register the category first.
debug:     [gratis-ai-agent] after registerCategory; getAbilityCategory result= Promise   ← smoking gun
\`\`\`

### Bug A — wrong \`registerAbility()\` signature

\`registry.js\` was calling the WP 7.0 API with two positional arguments:

\`\`\`js
wp.abilities.registerAbility( def.name, { label, description, ... } );  // WRONG
\`\`\`

The documented API takes a **single options object** whose \`name\` field identifies the ability. With positional args, the library reads \`.name\` off the options bag (undefined) and throws \`Ability name is required\`.

**Fix:** pass a single object.

\`\`\`js
wp.abilities.registerAbility( { name: def.name, label, description, ... } );
\`\`\`

### Bug B — \`registerAbilityCategory()\` missing required \`description\`

The category was registered with only a \`label\`. The WP 7.0 dev note documents \`description\` as required and the library throws \`The category properties must contain a description string\`.

**Fix:** add a description.

### Bug C — registration calls were synchronous (the actual root cause)

**The entire WP 7.0 abilities API is async.** Both \`registerAbility\` and \`registerAbilityCategory\` (and \`getAbilities\`, \`getAbilityCategory\`, etc.) return Promises. The registry code called them synchronously and immediately tried to register an ability into a category whose Promise had not yet resolved — so the ability lookup ran against an empty category index and threw \`Ability references non-existent category\`.

The smoking gun was a debug \`console.log\` I added during diagnosis:

\`\`\`text
[gratis-ai-agent] after registerCategory; getAbilityCategory result= Promise
\`\`\`

**Fix:** make \`registerCategory()\`, \`registerClientAbility()\`, \`registerNavigationAbility()\`, \`registerEditorAbility()\`, and \`ensureRegistered()\` all async, and \`await\` every API call. Use a single in-flight \`categoryRegistrationPromise\` so concurrent callers (multiple bundles on the same page, or duplicate \`ensureRegistered()\` calls) await the same registration instead of racing.

## Bonus fixes shipped together

Fixing the above surfaced two related issues that needed correcting in the same PR.

### Init order regression in \`src/abilities/index.js\`

\`navigation.js\` and \`editor.js\` were calling \`registerClientAbility(...)\` at module-eval time. ES-module hoisting evaluates these BEFORE \`registerCategory()\` runs in \`ensureRegistered()\`, so the abilities tried to register before the category existed even with my t166 fixes above.

**Fix:** refactor each module to export a \`register*Ability()\` function that \`ensureRegistered()\` awaits in the correct order. \`registerCategory()\` always runs (and its Promise resolves) before any \`registerClientAbility()\` call.

### \`snapshotDescriptors()\` was reading from the wrong store

\`snapshotDescriptors()\` previously read from \`wp.data.select('core/abilities').getAbilities()\`, but on WP 7.0-RC2 the \`@wordpress/data\` store mirror is **not** consistently populated by \`@wordpress/core-abilities\`. Verified in the browser:

| Source | Count |
|---|---|
| \`wp.abilities.getAbilities()\` (script-module API) | **62** ✅ |
| \`wp.data.select('core/abilities').getAbilities()\` | 0 ❌ |

**Fix:** read directly via the script-module API.

\`\`\`js
const allAbilities = ( await wp.abilities.getAbilities() ) || [];
\`\`\`

This makes the function async; \`sessionsSlice.sendMessage\` awaits it.

### \`sessionsSlice\` awaits \`ensureRegistered()\` before snapshotting

Previously \`sessionsSlice\` imported \`snapshotDescriptors\` from \`'../../abilities/registry'\` directly, which loads \`registry.js\` but **not** \`index.js\` — so \`ensureRegistered()\` never ran from the chat code path. Added an explicit import + \`await\` in the \`sendMessage\` thunk so the registration Promises are guaranteed to have resolved before we snapshot the descriptors to POST to \`/chat\`.

## Verified end-to-end in a real browser

Headless Playwright smoke test against the local WP 7.0-RC2 dev install:

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Test 3 (dashboard): \`wp.abilities.getAbilities()\` | **62 abilities** including \`gratis-ai-agent-js/navigate-to\` AND \`gratis-ai-agent-js/insert-block\` ✅ |
| Test 3 (dashboard): \`wp.abilities.getAbilityCategory('gratis-ai-agent-js')\` | category object with full metadata ✅ |
| Test 4 (dashboard): \`wp.abilities.executeAbility('gratis-ai-agent-js/navigate-to', { path: 'plugins.php' })\` | returned \`{ navigated: true, path: 'plugins.php' }\` AND **the browser actually navigated** to plugins.php ✅ |
| Test 5 (post-new): block editor screen sees both abilities | ✅ |
| Test 7: \`snapshotDescriptors()\` round-trip | returns 2 descriptors with correct shape — exactly what \`sessionsSlice\` will POST as \`client_abilities\` ✅ |
| Test 6: relevant console errors | **zero** — all previous \`Ability references non-existent category\` / \`Ability name is required\` / \`category properties must contain description\` errors are gone ✅ |

## Local gates

- \`npm run build\`: clean (pre-existing size warnings only)
- \`npx eslint src/abilities/ src/store/slices/sessionsSlice.js\`: zero errors
- \`npm run test:js\`: 214 pass / 31 fail — **identical** to clean main baseline. The 31 failures are pre-existing snapshot mismatches in \`MessageInput\`, \`ChatPanel\`, \`OnboardingWizard\`, \`ProviderSelector\`, \`ContextIndicator\` components, none of which this PR touches; tracked by t162.

## Out of scope (potential follow-ups)

- The \`core/abilities\` \`@wordpress/data\` store mirror is empty on WP 7.0-RC2. May be a missing \`@wordpress/core-abilities\` enqueue or a core RC2 issue. Not blocking because we use the script-module API directly. Worth re-checking on final 7.0.
- \`gratis-ai-agent-js/insert-block\` currently registers on every screen and the executeInsertBlock callback no-ops on non-editor pages via a \`wp.data.select('core/block-editor')\` guard. Could be improved by only registering when the editor is mounted, but that requires re-running registration when the editor mounts asynchronously — not a blocker, the callback guard is correct.

## Related

- Plan: #806
- Server-side implementation: #815 (merged)
- Entry-point wiring: #821 / t165 (merged)
- This PR: t166 — closes the runtime gap left by t165
- Smoke-test script: lives at \`/tmp/t165-smoke.mjs\` on dev workstation; should probably become a Playwright spec in a follow-up so CI can catch this class of regression

Resolves #806 (for the third and hopefully final time).

title: t169: enqueue @wordpress/core-abilities explicitly on admin pages
body:
## Summary

Fixes the `wp.data.select('core/abilities').getAbilities()` returning 0 items on WP 7.0-RC2 admin pages.

## Root Cause (t169 investigation)

The WP 7.0 dev note claims `@wordpress/core-abilities` is enqueued by core on all admin pages. **This is incorrect for RC2.** Inspection of the WordPress source confirms:

- `@wordpress/core-abilities` is **registered** in `wp-includes/js/dist/script-modules/registry.php`
- It is **never enqueued** — no `wp_enqueue_script_module('@wordpress/core-abilities')` call exists anywhere in WordPress core PHP

Evidence:
```php
// wp_script_modules()->queue after a stock admin page load (no plugins):
// → [] (empty — core-abilities is NOT in the queue)

// After our explicit enqueue:
wp_enqueue_script_module('@wordpress/core-abilities');
// → ["@wordpress/abilities", "@wordpress/core-abilities"] ✓
```

Without the enqueue, the `@wordpress/core-abilities` JS module never loads, so the REST fetch to `/wp-abilities/v1/abilities` never runs, and the `core/abilities` Redux store stays empty.

## What Changed

- **`includes/Admin/FloatingWidget.php`**: Add `wp_enqueue_script_module('@wordpress/core-abilities')` alongside the existing `@wordpress/abilities` enqueue
- **`includes/Admin/ScreenMetaPanel.php`**: Same
- **`includes/Admin/UnifiedAdminMenu.php`**: Same
- **`src/abilities/registry.js`**: Update `snapshotDescriptors()` comment with confirmed root cause, evidence, and a TODO to revisit after WP 7.0 final ships

## Testing

Verified at PHP level:
```php
wp_enqueue_script_module('@wordpress/core-abilities');
// Queue now contains: ["@wordpress/abilities", "@wordpress/core-abilities"]
```

The `@wordpress/core-abilities` module fetches from `/wp-abilities/v1/abilities` (REST endpoint confirmed registered and returning data) and calls `registerAbility()` for each server ability, which dispatches to the `core/abilities` Redux store.

After this fix, `wp.data.select('core/abilities').getAbilities()` should return the same count as `wp.abilities.getAbilities()` on any admin page where our plugin loads.

## Runtime Testing

Risk: **Medium** (script module enqueue, no data deletion, no auth changes). No dev environment available for browser-level verification in this headless session. The PHP-level queue verification confirms the enqueue path is correct.

## Resolves

Resolves #825

title: Fix empty `properties` schemas serialising as JSON `[]` not `{}`
body:
## Summary

`gratis_ai_agent_normalize_ability_schema()` was injecting `'properties' => []` (PHP empty array) into object-typed schemas in three places. When JSON-encoded, that becomes `[]` (array), violating JSON Schema. The OpenAI-compatible tool-schema validator in Ollama then crashes with:

```
Bad Request (400) - Value looks like object, but can't find closing '}' symbol
```

The error fires **before** the model is invoked, so **every tool-using request returned 400 in <1ms** — the agent could not call any abilities against an Ollama-backed provider until this fix.

## Root cause

`ability-call`'s `arguments` field is declared as `{type: object, description: ...}` with no `properties` key. The normalizer's "object schemas must have a properties field" branch (line 193-195) added `'properties' => []`. JSON-encoded this becomes `[]` not `{}`, and Ollama's Go-side schema walker treats it as a malformed object.

The author already used `(object) []` correctly in the `wp_register_ability_args` fallback below — this fix just applies the same pattern in the recursive normalizer.

## Changes

Three sites in `gratis-ai-agent.php`:
- L148-153: top-level empty schema fallback
- L165-169: empty `properties` in existing object schema
- L192-195: object schema missing `properties` (the actual trigger)

All now use `(object) []` so JSON encoding emits `{}`.

## Verification

Tested live against `qwen3.5:latest` on Ollama (`ultimate-ai-connector-compatible-endpoints`). Before fix: 100% of tool-using requests fail with 400 in 200µs. After fix:

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Math, no tools | OK (391) |
| List recent posts | OK via run-php |
| Count installed plugins | OK via get-plugins (50) |
| Site title + tagline | OK, two parallel tool calls |
| DB user count | OK via db-query |

Discovered while running a test battery requested by the user. Found via tool-by-tool bisection of the captured request body.

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)

1. Cosmetic `Undefined array key "type"` warnings from `rest-api.php:2214/2229/2238` — pre-existing, surfaced now that requests reach validation. Worth a separate look.
2. There is no debug-mode feature for capturing outbound LLM provider requests/responses. I had to drop a temporary mu-plugin to debug this. Worth adding so future provider issues are easier to diagnose.
3. `run-php` description doesn't strongly steer models toward associative-array args for functions like `wp_insert_post`; a test prompt to "create a draft post" caused qwen3.5 to call it with positional args. `ai-agent/create-post` exists but isn't in `DEFAULT_TIER_1` so the model didn't see it without an `ability-search` first.

title: Steer model away from `run-php` toward dedicated abilities
body:
## Summary

Stops smaller local models (observed with `qwen3.5:latest` on Ollama) from defaulting to `run-php` + wrong positional args when a dedicated ability already exists.

Two changes working together:

**(a)** Add `ai-agent/create-post` to `DEFAULT_TIER_1`. \"Create a post\" is the most obvious WordPress operation and belongs in cold-start so the model sees it without a prior `ability-search` round-trip. The ~200 prompt-token cost is worth eliminating the positional-args failure mode on `wp_insert_post`.

**(b)** Rewrite `run-php`'s description (all three registration sites — `handle_run_php`, `register` override, and `RunPhpAbility::description`) to explicitly frame it as a **low-level fallback**, list the common operations with dedicated abilities, and direct the model to `ability-search` first. The previous description was a neutral \"Call a whitelisted WordPress function\" which models happily reached for as a first-resort hammer.

## Before / after

Same prompt: *\"Create a draft post titled 'AI Agent Test Post' with body ... Reply with the new post ID.\"*

**Before** (`DEFAULT_TIER_1` without `create-post`, generic `run-php` description):
```
[1] run-php(wp_insert_post, ["AI Agent Test Post","...","draft"])
    => error: empty_content (positional args, not associative)
[2] ability-search("create post insert")
    => finds ai-agent/create-post
... out of iterations, no post created
```

**After**:
```
[1] ai-agent/create-post({"title":"...","content":"...","status":"draft"})
    => {"post_id":14, ...}
Done in 1 tool call.
```

## Changes

- `includes/Tools/ToolDiscovery.php` — add `ai-agent/create-post` to `DEFAULT_TIER_1` with a comment explaining why.
- `includes/Abilities/WordPressAbilities.php` — update all three `run-php` description sites to the new fallback-framing wording.

## Verification

Tested live against `qwen3.5:latest` on Ollama via `wp ai-agent`. Post 14 created as a draft in a single tool call with correct associative-array arguments.

Resolves #831

Resolves #830

## What Changed

- `includes/Models/ProviderTrace.php` — Data model with ring-buffered storage, credential redaction, body truncation, and curl command generation
- `includes/Core/ProviderTraceLogger.php` — Hooks `pre_http_request` + `http_response` to capture traffic to known AI provider endpoints (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Ollama) only when tracing is enabled
- `includes/REST/TraceController.php` — REST API endpoints: `GET /trace` (list), `GET /trace/{id}` (detail), `GET /trace/{id}/curl`, `DELETE /trace` (clear), `GET/POST /trace/settings`
- `includes/CLI/TraceCommand.php` — WP-CLI: `wp ai-agent trace list|show|clear|enable|disable|status`
- `src/settings-page/provider-trace-viewer.js` — React admin UI with list view, filters (provider, errors-only), detail modal with side-by-side request/response JSON viewer, and copy-as-curl button

### Modified Files
- `includes/Core/Database.php` — Added `provider_trace` table schema, bumped DB version to 14.0.0
- `includes/Core/Settings.php` — Added `provider_trace_enabled` and `provider_trace_max_rows` defaults
- `gratis-ai-agent.php` — Registered ProviderTraceLogger, TraceController REST routes, and TraceCommand CLI
- `src/settings-page/settings-app.js` — Added "Provider Trace" tab to settings

## Key Design Decisions

1. **Off by default** — Tracing is disabled by default with a prominent warning when enabled ("logs may contain prompt content")
2. **Ring buffer** — Oldest rows auto-deleted when max (default 200) is reached, preventing unbounded table growth
3. **Credential redaction** — Authorization headers, API keys, Bearer tokens, and sensitive JSON keys are redacted before storage
4. **Body truncation** — Request/response bodies truncated at 64KB to prevent storage bloat
5. **Filter override** — `gratis_ai_agent_provider_trace_enabled` filter allows enabling tracing environmentally without touching settings
6. **Provider matching** — Uses URL host matching against known provider endpoints; extensible via `gratis_ai_agent_trace_match_provider` filter

- PHP syntax verified for all new/modified files

- ESLint passes on new JS file

title: feat: add Agent Capabilities v1 benchmark suite for complex model evaluation
body:
## Summary

Adds a new benchmark suite (`agent-capabilities-v1`) with 15 open-ended questions designed to differentiate capable models (like Opus) from simpler ones. The existing multiple-choice WordPress knowledge suite remains unchanged.

### What's new

**New benchmark suite** with 5 question categories:
- **Code Generation** (4 questions): REST API endpoints, shortcodes with WP_Query/pagination, dbDelta table creation, Gutenberg blocks with InspectorControls, circuit breaker pattern
- **Debugging** (3 questions): Security audit of save_post handler (5+ bugs), SQL injection + data exposure in REST endpoint, WSOD memory exhaustion diagnosis
- **Reasoning** (2 questions): Performance diagnosis methodology for 50K-post site, editorial workflow design using WordPress primitives
- **Architecture** (2 questions): WooCommerce-to-CRM sync with rate limiting/retry/batching, multisite shared announcements data model with trade-off analysis
- **Multi-step** (3 questions): Full security audit of AJAX handler (7+ vulnerabilities), WP-CLI data migration with batching/dry-run, REST API middleware system

**Enhanced benchmark engine:**
- New `open_ended` question type with weighted keyword scoring (0-100 partial credit)
- Category-aware prompt building with tailored system instructions per question type
- Dynamic `max_tokens`: 10 for multiple-choice, 1500-2048 for open-ended
- Scaled HTTP timeouts (120s) for longer model responses
- Google Gemini `generationConfig.maxOutputTokens` support

### How scoring works

Each open-ended question defines `scoring_criteria`: an array of keyword patterns with weights. Keywords support pipe-separated alternatives (e.g., `sanitize_text_field|esc_html`) and are matched case-insensitively. The score is the sum of matched weights normalized to 0-100. A score >= 60 is considered "passing" for binary comparison, but the numeric score provides granular model differentiation.

### Backward compatibility

- Existing `wp-core-v1` and `wp-quick` suites are unchanged
- The `knowledge` question type evaluation is unchanged (binary correct/incorrect)
- No database schema changes required
- No frontend changes needed (the benchmark page dynamically renders suites from the API)

- PHPStan level 10: 0 errors on both files

title: fix: use sentinel object for get_option existence checks in OptionsAbilities
body:
## Summary

Fixes the edge case where WordPress options storing a literal `false` value are misdetected as non-existent in `UpdateOptionAbility` and `DeleteOptionAbility`.

## Problem

Both classes used `false !== get_option( $option_name, false )` to check option existence. When an option's stored value is boolean `false`, `get_option()` returns `false` — identical to the default — making it impossible to distinguish "option exists with value false" from "option does not exist".

## Fix

Replace the `false` default with a unique `stdClass` sentinel object. Since no stored option value can ever be the same object instance, a strict `!==` comparison against the sentinel reliably detects non-existence:

```php
$sentinel = new \stdClass();
$exists   = get_option( $option_name, $sentinel ) !== $sentinel;
```

Applied to both:
- `UpdateOptionAbility::execute_callback()` (~line 333) — prevents false "unchanged" reports
- `DeleteOptionAbility::execute_callback()` (~line 443) — prevents false "not_found" reports

## Runtime Testing

Risk level: **Low** — logic-only fix, no API surface changes, no new dependencies.

Self-assessed: the sentinel pattern is a well-established PHP idiom for this exact WordPress API limitation. PHPCS passes with zero violations.

Resolves #866

title: feat: async job architecture with live tool progress
body:
## Summary

- Replace synchronous `/chat` endpoint with async `/run` + `/job/{id}` polling to eliminate nginx/proxy gateway timeouts on long-running agent loops
- Add live tool call progress in the chat UI — users see which tools are running instead of just "Thinking..."
- Fix duplicate response messages and per-session job isolation
- Bundle WP-CLI ability (`wp-cli/execute`) directly into the plugin

## Architecture change

**Before:** Browser sends `POST /chat` → PHP runs the full agent loop synchronously → returns response. Any proxy with a 60s timeout kills the connection.

**After:** Browser sends `POST /run` → PHP creates a job transient, fires a non-blocking loopback to `/process`, returns `202 Accepted` with a `job_id` immediately. The `/process` handler calls `fastcgi_finish_request()` to detach from HTTP, then runs the agent loop in the background. Browser polls `GET /job/{id}` every 3s for progress and the final result.

## Changes

### Backend (PHP)
- **`RestController.php`**: Removed `/chat` route registration (returns 410 stub). Made `upload_attachments_to_media_library()` public for SessionController access.
- **`SessionController.php`**: Updated `/run` to accept `attachments` and `client_abilities`. Added `fastcgi_finish_request()` in `/process` to survive client disconnect. Added progress callback that writes `tool_calls` to job transient in real-time. Wrapped loop execution in `try/catch (\Throwable)` so crashes surface as error messages instead of hanging. Updated `handle_job_status` to return `tool_calls` for all statuses.
- **`AgentLoop.php`**: Added `progress_callback` option — callable invoked after each `log_tool_calls()` and `log_tool_responses()`.
- **`WpCliAbilities.php`** (new): Moved `wp-cli/execute` ability from external `cli-abilities-bridge` plugin. Includes tokenizer, command blocklist, permission classification, and `proc_open` executor.
- **`ToolDiscovery.php`**: Replaced `run-php` with `wp-cli/execute` in `DEFAULT_TIER_1`.

### Frontend (JS/CSS)
- **`sessionsSlice.js`**: `streamMessage` now POSTs to `/run` and starts `pollJob`. `pollJob` reloads session from DB on completion (fixes duplicates). Added `sessionJobs` map for per-session job tracking. Added `liveToolCalls` state + `setLiveToolCalls` action.
- **`message-list.js`**: Added `LiveToolProgress` component showing "Running `wp-cli/execute` (4)", "3 tools completed", "Composing reply..." inside the thinking bubble.
- **`session-sidebar.js`**: Added pulsing blue dot badge on sessions with active background jobs.
- **CSS**: Styles for live progress indicator and session job badge.

## Testing

Tested in browser with multi-tool prompts (4+ WP-CLI calls). Verified:
- No gateway timeouts (response returns in <2s, processing continues in background)
- Live tool progress updates every 3s poll cycle
- No duplicate messages on completion
- Switching sessions doesn't show "Thinking" on wrong chat
- Errors from crashed tools surface properly instead of hanging

title: fix: raise AI Client SDK timeout to 120s for agentic workloads
body:
## Problem

Prompts like _"research AIDS and write a current blog post article"_ fail with:

```
Error: Network error occurred while sending request to https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages:
cURL error 28: Operation timed out after 30002 milliseconds with 0 bytes received
```

**Root cause:** The WordPress AI Client SDK applies a **30-second HTTP timeout** via the `wp_ai_client_default_request_timeout` filter (default: `30`, set in `class-wp-ai-client-prompt-builder.php:200`). The final generation call for a research + long-form article can take 30–60 seconds, hitting this limit before the response arrives.

The agent loop already enforces a 120-second wall-clock budget (`AgentLoop::LOOP_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`), but the HTTP layer was cutting the connection at 30s — well before the loop's own deadline.

## Fix

Hook `wp_ai_client_default_request_timeout` in `gratis-ai-agent.php` to return `AgentLoop::LOOP_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` (120s), aligning the HTTP timeout with the loop's own wall-clock budget:

```php
add_filter(
    'wp_ai_client_default_request_timeout',
    static function (): int {
        return AgentLoop::LOOP_TIMEOUT_SECONDS; // 120
    }
);
```

The background worker (`/process` endpoint) already calls `set_time_limit(600)`, so PHP execution time is not a constraint. This change only raises the cURL/HTTP layer timeout to match what the loop already allows.

## Testing

Reproduce with the prompt that was failing:
> "research AIDS and write a current blog post article about how well it is being treated"

Before this fix: times out at ~30s with cURL error 28.  
After this fix: completes and returns a full article (typically 40–90s depending on model and output length).

title: t881: fix progress callback transient TTL to prevent mid-execution expiry
body:
## Summary

Resolves #881

The progress callback in `SessionController.php` wrote tool-call activity to a WordPress transient so the polling frontend could display incremental updates. However, `JOB_TTL` (600s) matches `set_time_limit` (600s), meaning the transient could expire before a long-running job completed — causing `get_transient()` to return `false` and the final job result to silently vanish.

## Changes

**File**: `includes/REST/SessionController.php:1263-1283`

Two fixes applied to the `$options['progress_callback']` closure:

1. **TTL buffer on refresh** — Changed `JOB_TTL` to `JOB_TTL + 60` (660s) on each progress update. This ensures the transient outlasts the execution limit even when the callback fires near the end of the job.

2. **Expired transient recovery** — Added an `elseif ( false === $current )` branch. When the transient has already expired, a minimal `['status' => 'processing', 'tool_calls' => ...]` entry is re-created so the final job result can still be persisted after loop completion.

## Runtime Testing

**Risk**: Low — defensive code path that only fires in edge cases (long jobs near the 600s execution limit). No behaviour change for normal jobs.

**Self-assessed**: Logic is straightforward transient read/write. The fix mirrors the pattern used throughout `RestController.php` and `SessionController.php` for transient management.

- PHPCS: clean (`composer phpcs -- includes/REST/SessionController.php`)
- PHPStan: clean, No errors (`composer phpstan -- includes/REST/SessionController.php`)

`gratis-ai-agent.php` references `AgentLoop::LOOP_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` inside a static closure registered as a filter:

```php
);
```

All other `GratisAiAgent\Core` classes are imported via `use` statements (lines 90–97), but `AgentLoop` was missing. PHP resolves unqualified class names in the global namespace, so `AgentLoop` fails with class-not-found.

title: fix: align E2E test port with .wp-env.json (8890 not 8888)
body:
## Summary

All E2E test shards have been failing consistently because `wp-env` starts on port **8890** (per `.wp-env.json`), but the workflow readiness check, `WP_BASE_URL`, Playwright config, and test files all hardcoded port **8888**. The readiness check polled a port where nothing was listening, timing out after 30 attempts on every shard.

## Changes

- **`.github/workflows/e2e.yml`**: Updated `wp_env_port` matrix values from `8888` to `8890`. Replaced hardcoded port in readiness check and `WP_BASE_URL` with `${{ matrix.wp_env_port }}` for maintainability.
- **`playwright.config.js`**: Updated default `baseURL` fallback from `8888` to `8890` to match `.wp-env.json`.
- **`tests/e2e/shared-conversations.spec.js`**: Updated 5 `baseURL` fallbacks from `8888` to `8890`.
- **`tests/e2e/agent-builder.spec.js`**: Updated example URL in JSDoc comment.

## Root Cause

`.wp-env.json` defines `"port": 8890` for the dev site. The CI workflow was written with port `8888` (the wp-env default when no port is specified), creating a mismatch. The `wp_env_port` matrix variable was defined but never actually used in any step — it was dead config.

## Evidence

From the [latest failed run](https://github.com/Ultimate-Multisite/gratis-ai-agent/actions/runs/24419947113) logs:
```
WordPress development site started at http://localhost:8890
```
Immediately followed by:

```
wp-env did not become ready in time
```

title: feat: Plugin Builder & Sandbox System — AI-powered plugin generation with safe activation
body:
## Summary

Implements the Plugin Builder & Sandbox System from issue #912 (Phase 1 + Phase 2 + Phase 3 ability registration).

### What was built

**Three-layer sandbox safety model:**
- **Layer 1** (`PluginSandbox::layer1_syntax_check`): `php -l` on every generated PHP file — cheap, instant, catches ~60% of fatal errors.
- **Layer 2** (`PluginSandbox::layer2_isolated_include`): WP-CLI subprocess `eval-file` with `--skip-plugins`. If fatal, only the subprocess dies.
- **Layer 3** (`PluginSandbox::layer3_activate`): `activate_plugin()` with a pre-activation transient guard + shutdown function. Auto-deactivates on next request if a fatal was caught.

**New classes under `includes/PluginBuilder/`:**
- `PluginSandbox.php` — three-layer safety system
- `PluginGenerator.php` — plan + code generation via `wp_ai_client_prompt()`
- `PluginInstaller.php` — write files to `wp-content/plugins/`, track in `gratis_ai_agent_generated_plugins` DB table
- `PluginUpdater.php` — backup → stage → sandbox test → swap flow for live updates
- `HookScanner.php` — regex-based hook discovery (`do_action`, `apply_filters`, `add_action`, `add_filter`) in plugins and themes

**Six new abilities registered via `wp_register_ability()`:**
- `gratis-ai-agent/generate-plugin` — full generate+install flow
- `gratis-ai-agent/sandbox-test-plugin` — layers 1+2 only
- `gratis-ai-agent/sandbox-activate-plugin` — layer 3 transactional activation
- `gratis-ai-agent/update-plugin-sandboxed` — sandboxed live updates
- `gratis-ai-agent/scan-plugin-hooks` — scan installed plugin for hooks
- `gratis-ai-agent/scan-theme-hooks` — scan installed theme for hooks

**Database:**
- `DB_VERSION` bumped to `15.0.0`
- New table `{prefix}gratis_ai_agent_generated_plugins` with columns: `id`, `slug`, `description`, `plan`, `plugin_file`, `files`, `status`, `sandbox_result`, `activation_error`, `created_at`, `updated_at`

### Testing

All PHP files pass `php -l` syntax check. The `PluginBuilderAbilities` register via the `wp_abilities_api_init` hook consistent with all other ability classes. The `PluginSandbox::auto_deactivate_fatal_plugins` runs on `init` to clean up any plugins flagged via transient guard.

Resolves #912

title: t918: PluginUpdater — sandboxed live updates to running plugins
body:
## Summary

Implements the `PluginUpdater` class (#918) — sandboxed live updates for AI-generated plugins using the backup → stage → test → swap → verify → rollback pattern.

## Changes

- **EDIT**: `includes/PluginBuilder/PluginUpdater.php` — complete rewrite from static-method prototype to instance-based API matching the issue specification
- **NEW**: `tests/GratisAiAgent/PluginBuilder/PluginUpdaterTest.php` — 14 unit tests covering all public methods

### API delivered

```php
public function backup(string $slug): string|WP_Error
public function stage(string $slug, array $modified_files): string|WP_Error
public function test_staged(string $slug, string $staging_dir): array
public function swap(string $slug, string $staging_dir, string $backup_dir): array|WP_Error
public function rollback(string $slug, string $backup_dir): array|WP_Error
public function cleanup_old_backups(int $max_age_days = 7): int
public function update(string $slug, array $modified_files): array|WP_Error
```

### Key implementation notes

- Backups land in `wp-content/gratis-ai-backups/{slug}-{timestamp}/`
- Staging uses `wp-content/gratis-ai-staging/{slug}/`
- `stage()` copies the live plugin first then overlays modified files — the staged copy is always complete
- `swap()` uses `WP_Filesystem::move()` (not `rename()`) per WPCS; restores backup automatically on reactivation failure
- `cleanup_old_backups()` respects `gratis_ai_agent_backup_retention_days` filter; always preserves the most recent backup regardless of age
- PHPStan level 5 clean; PHPCS WordPress standards clean

## Testing

```bash
composer phpstan
composer phpcs
npm run test:php  # requires wp-env
```

Resolves #918

## Summary

```php
public function backup(string $slug): string|WP_Error
public function stage(string $slug, array $modified_files): string|WP_Error
public function test_staged(string $slug, string $staging_dir): array
public function swap(string $slug, string $staging_dir, string $backup_dir): array|WP_Error

public function cleanup_old_backups(int $max_age_days = 7): int
```

title: fix: HookScanner empty-slug guard and test slug sanitization
body:
## Summary

Two bugs exposed by the new unit tests added in #933 and #932:

**Bug 1 — empty slug bypasses WP_Error guard**  
`scan_plugin('')`/`scan_theme('')` called `sanitize_title('')` → `''` → checked `is_dir('/plugins//')` which resolved to the real `plugins/` directory and returned an array of all plugin hooks instead of `WP_Error`. Fix: add explicit `empty()` guard after `sanitize_title()`.

**Bug 2 — `uniqid('', true)` dot in test slugs causes path mismatch**  
`uniqid('', true)` includes a microsecond float like `abc.12345`. `sanitize_title()` converts `.` → `-`, so the directory created by `make_temp_plugin()` and the path looked up by `HookScanner::scan_plugin()` diverge. Fix: strip the dot suffix from slugs in test helpers so the directory name matches what `sanitize_title()` will produce.

## Changes

- `includes/PluginBuilder/HookScanner.php`: add `empty($plugin_slug)` guard in `scan_plugin()` and `scan_theme()` before `is_dir()` check
- `tests/GratisAiAgent/PluginBuilder/HookScannerTest.php`: strip `.` from `uniqid('', true)` results in `make_temp_plugin()` and `make_temp_theme()` helpers

## Verification

```bash
composer phpstan   # 0 errors
composer phpcs     # 0 errors
npm run test:php   # HookScannerTest passes (was 11 failures before this fix)
```

Resolves the 11 test failures in #933 CI and the pre-existing failures from #932.

## Summary

Implements the `report-inability` ability (t185) so the AI agent can self-flag when it cannot complete a user request. This is part of the customer feedback & issue reporting system (t180-t187).

### What was built

- **`includes/Abilities/FeedbackAbilities.php`** (new): Registers the `gratis-ai-agent/report-inability` ability with schema `{ reason: string, attempted_steps?: string[] }`. The execute handler sets a request-scoped static flag (`self::$inability_data`) that persists within the PHP request lifecycle.

- **`includes/Core/AgentLoop.php`**: Added `inject_inability_data()` private helper that merges the inability flag into loop result arrays at the two normal exit points (text reply and fallback summarisation). Added `FeedbackAbilities` import. Extended `default_system_instruction()` with a "Reporting Inability" section instructing the model to call the ability after genuinely exhausting 2+ approaches.

- **`includes/REST/RestController.php`**: Passes `inability_reported` field through in the REST response (mirrors the existing `exit_reason` passthrough pattern).

- **`gratis-ai-agent.php`**: Imports and registers `FeedbackAbilities`.

- **`src/store/slices/sessionsSlice.js`**: Adds `inabilityReported` state field, `setInabilityReported` action, `SET_INABILITY_REPORTED` reducer case, and `getInabilityReported` selector. Detects `inability_reported` in the job-poll completion handler and stores it. Clears the flag when the user sends a new message.

- **`src/components/message-list.js`**: Renders a dismissible inline banner ("The AI was unable to complete your request.") when `inabilityReported` is truthy and not currently sending. Dismiss clears the Redux state.

### Architecture notes

The inability flag travels the same path as the existing `exit_reason` field:
`FeedbackAbilities::handle_report_inability()` → static flag → `AgentLoop::inject_inability_data()` → result array → `RestController` REST response → `sessionsSlice` job-poll handler → React `message-list` banner.

The "Send Report" button is intentionally absent from this PR — the `FeedbackConsentModal` (t182) and report sender (t181) are prerequisites for that flow. This PR delivers the detection and surface layer; the action wiring follows in t182/t183.

### Verification

title: t182: Consent UI — payload preview, stats, strip-tool-results, REST endpoint
body:
## What

Implements t182: the full feedback consent modal + the server-side infrastructure it depends on.

**PHP (new files — `includes/Feedback/`):**

- `ReportBuilder.php` — collects session messages, tool calls, token counts, and environment metadata (WP version, PHP version, plugin version, theme, active plugins, locale, is_multisite, site_host). `strip_tool_results` flag redacts output while keeping tool names/arguments. `build_summary()` returns lightweight stats for the modal header.
- `ReportSanitizer.php` — sender-side sanitizer strips credentials (Bearer tokens, API keys, AWS keys, JWT, etc.) and absolute server paths before transmission. Defense-in-depth complement to the receiver-side sanitizer.
- `ReportSender.php` — `wp_remote_post()` to the configured endpoint with `X-Feedback-Api-Key` header; graceful error handling (returns `WP_Error`, never crashes).

**REST (new `includes/REST/FeedbackController.php`):**

- `GET /gratis-ai-agent/v1/feedback/preview` — returns sanitized payload + summary stats for the consent modal's collapsible preview section.
- `POST /gratis-ai-agent/v1/feedback/send` — builds, sanitizes, and forwards the report; accepts `session_id`, `report_type`, `user_description`, `strip_tool_results`.

**`includes/REST/RestController.php`:** registers `FeedbackController::register_routes()`.

**JS (`src/components/feedback-consent-modal.js`):**

Full t182 feature set on top of the minimal t184 modal:
1. Summary stats (message count, tool calls, environment key count, model) fetched from `/feedback/preview`
2. Collapsible "View full payload" section showing the sanitized JSON
3. "Strip tool results" checkbox (aggressive privacy mode) — refetches preview on toggle
4. Passes `session_id` and `strip_tool_results` to `POST /feedback/send`

**Callers (`message-input.js`, `message-list.js`):** pass `sessionId={currentSessionId}` to the modal.

**`src/components/shared.css`:** styles for stats bar, strip-label, payload toggle + pre block.

## Testing

- PHP syntax: `php -l` passes on all 4 new PHP files
- ESLint: zero violations on `feedback-consent-modal.js`, `message-input.js`, `message-list.js`
- Stylelint: zero violations on `shared.css`
- Jest: all 36 `MessageInput` tests pass (including 4 FeedbackConsentModal tests from t184)
- Runtime: `self-assessed` — no local wp-env available; REST endpoints and JS component are straightforward CRUD with existing patterns

## Key decisions

- Preview endpoint (`GET /feedback/preview`) separates the "show me what will be sent" concern from the "send it" concern — the modal fetches this on open and re-fetches on `stripToolResults` toggle so the displayed JSON always matches what gets sent.
- `session_id=0` in the POST body is treated as "no session" and sends a minimal payload; callers that have no session (e.g. onboarding) don't crash.
- PHP classes placed under `includes/Feedback/` (new subdirectory) to match the PSR-4 namespace `GratisAiAgent\Feedback\*` — no `composer.json` changes needed.

title: fix: tool confirmation dialog styling, stdClass crash, and confirmation UX
body:
## Summary

- **Tool confirmation dialog unstyled**: `wp-scripts` splits CSS into `style-{entry}.css` and `{entry}.css`. Only `style-*.css` was enqueued; `admin-page.css` and `floating-widget.css` containing the overlay/dialog styles from `shared.css` were never loaded. Now both are enqueued.
- **`Cannot use object of type stdClass as array` crash**: AI providers may return `stdClass` objects for JSON function-call arguments. `WP_Ability::execute()` passes input to callbacks without converting `stdClass` → array. Added `do_execute()` override in `AbstractAbility` that recursively normalizes `stdClass` to arrays before any callback runs. Also hardened `AbilityFunctionResolver` and `ToolDiscovery::handle_ability_call` as defense-in-depth.
- **Background worker errors silently swallowed**: The try/catch in `SessionController` stored the error message in the job transient but never wrote to `debug.log`. Added `error_log()` with full stack trace so these errors are diagnosable.
- **Non-destructive abilities requiring confirmation**: The classification was binary (`read` vs `write`). Now uses three tiers (`read`/`write`/`destructive`) based on the `readonly` and `destructive` annotations. Non-destructive writes like memory-save, install-plugin, create-post auto-execute; destructive operations (deletions, resets) still require confirmation.

## Changes

| File | What |
|---|---|
| `includes/Admin/UnifiedAdminMenu.php` | Enqueue `build/admin-page.css` |
| `includes/Admin/FloatingWidget.php` | Enqueue `build/floating-widget.css` |
| `includes/Abilities/AbstractAbility.php` | Override `do_execute()` with `stdClass` → array normalization |
| `includes/Core/AbilityFunctionResolver.php` | Add `normalize_args()` for recursive stdClass conversion |
| `includes/Tools/ToolDiscovery.php` | JSON round-trip normalization in `handle_ability_call` |
| `includes/Core/AgentLoop.php` | Three-tier `classify_ability()` using `destructive` annotation |
| `includes/REST/SessionController.php` | Log exceptions to `debug.log` with stack trace |
| `tests/GratisAiAgent/Core/AgentLoopTest.php` | Updated classify tests, added destructive/null cases |

## Testing

- PHP syntax clean on all changed files

title: fix(e2e): add processingPolls to interceptStream for timing-safe stop-button test
body:
## Summary

- Adds a `processingPolls` option (default `0`) to `interceptStream()` in `tests/e2e/chat-interactions.spec.js`
- The job route handler now returns `status: 'processing'` for the first `processingPolls` polls before switching to `status: 'complete'`
- Updates the stop-button test to use `processingPolls: 1`, preventing the race where an immediate `'complete'` response clears `sending` state before the assertion fires

## Problem

The `interceptStream` helper always returned `status: 'complete'` on the first poll. The 'stop button appears while sending' test asserts that the stop button is visible within 5 s — but a fast `'complete'` response can clear `sending=false` before the assertion window.

## Fix

```diff
-const { generatedTitle } = options;
+const { generatedTitle, processingPolls = 0 } = options;
+let jobPollCount = 0;
```

The job handler now gates completion on `jobPollCount > processingPolls`, giving timing-sensitive tests a controllable window to observe transient UI state.

## Verification

E2E test suite: `npm run test:e2e:playwright` — the 'stop button appears while sending' test is the primary regression target.

Resolves #965

title: fix: remove hard-coded session_id from E2E upload-clear job mock
body:
## Summary

Removes the hard-coded `session_id: 1` from the mocked job response in the E2E test `'attachments are cleared after sending a message'` in `tests/e2e/chat-upload.spec.js`.

When `session_id` is present in the mock job result, the Redux store treats it as authoritative and triggers a reload of `/gratis-ai-agent/v1/sessions/1`. This makes the test depend on whether session ID 1 exists in the wp-env database — causing failures for reasons unrelated to attachment clearing.

The fix omits `session_id` from the fulfilled body entirely so the store does not attempt a session reload, and the test remains focused on its actual assertion: that attachments are cleared after sending.

## Changes

- **EDIT**: `tests/e2e/chat-upload.spec.js:546` — removed `session_id: 1` from the mock job response body

## Testing

The test still verifies that `getAttachmentPreviews()` is not visible after sending — no functional logic changed, only the mock data.

Resolves #966

title: GH#975: fix E2E shard-2 flaky failures — chat-interactions and client-abilities
body:
## Summary

Fixes three root causes for consistent E2E shard 2 failures on `main` and across PRs:

1. **`registry.js` race condition** — `registerCategory()` returned early with `undefined` when `floating-widget.js` (regular deferred script) ran before `@wordpress/core-abilities` (script module with implicit defer) had populated `wp.abilities`. This left `categoryRegistrationPromise` null and abilities silently unregistered.

2. **`networkidle` timeout** — `goToDashboard()` in `client-abilities.spec.js` used `waitForLoadState('networkidle')` which consumed 60-70 s on loaded CI runners (floating widget makes 4+ async API calls), exhausting the 90 s test budget before `waitForAbilitiesRegistered` could run.

3. **`waitForFunction` wrong timeout argument** — `waitForAbilitiesRegistered` passed `{ timeout }` as the `arg` parameter (second argument) instead of the `options` parameter (third argument). The 15 s timeout was ignored; the full 90 s test timeout applied instead.

4. **Auto-title session tests** — After the mocked job completes, the store calls `fetchSessions()` and `GET /sessions/:id` against the real server. On loaded CI runners, these real REST calls can take 2-3 s each, pushing the total wait past the 10 s `toBeVisible` assertion timeout. The `.gratis-ai-agent-session-item.is-active` element never appeared.

## Changes

### `src/abilities/registry.js`
- Add `waitForAbilitiesApi()` — polls up to 10 s for `wp.abilities` to become available
- Set `categoryRegistrationPromise` before the first `await` to prevent concurrent racing
- Remove the early `return undefined` path that silently skipped registration

### `tests/e2e/client-abilities.spec.js`
- Replace `waitForLoadState('networkidle')` with `.gratis-ai-agent-fab` element wait in `goToDashboard()`
- Fix `waitForAbilitiesRegistered()` to pass `null` as arg and `{ timeout }` as options (third argument) to `page.waitForFunction()`

### `tests/e2e/chat-interactions.spec.js`
- Extend `interceptStream()` to also mock `GET /sessions/:id` (session reload) and `GET /sessions` (list) after `capturedSessionId` is captured. Routes pass through to the real server when `capturedSessionId` is null (initial fetch before job runs) so `goToAgentPage`'s `sessionsResponsePromise` is not broken.

### Build artifacts
- Rebuilt `floating-widget.js`, `admin-page.js`, `screen-meta.js`, `unified-admin.js` to include the `waitForAbilitiesApi` fix.

## Verification

The session mocks in `interceptStream` are conditional on `capturedSessionId !== null`, so:
- The initial `fetchSessions()` (during `goToAgentPage`) passes through to the real server — `goToAgentPage`'s `waitForResponse` still fires correctly.
- Only post-job `fetchSessions()` and session-reload calls return mock responses, making assertions on `.is-active` and session titles deterministic.

Resolves #975

body:
## Summary

Fixes two remaining root causes for consistent E2E shard 2 failures on \`main\` and across PRs. The registry.js race condition and \`goToDashboard\` networkidle replacement were already applied in #957.

### Root causes fixed

**1. Incorrect \`waitForFunction\` timeout argument — \`client-abilities.spec.js\`**

\`waitForAbilitiesRegistered\` called \`page.waitForFunction(fn, { timeout })\`. Playwright's API is \`waitForFunction(fn, arg?, options?)\` — the second argument is \`arg\` (data passed to the function), not the options object. The 15 s timeout was silently ignored; the full 90 s test timeout applied instead. This caused the \`page.waitForFunction timeout 90000ms\` error in CI: the abilities genuinely never registered AND the test had to exhaust the full test budget before surfacing the error.

Fix: \`page.waitForFunction(fn, null, { timeout })\`

**2. Auto-title session tests race against real REST calls — \`chat-interactions.spec.js\`**

After the mocked job completes, the store calls \`fetchSessions()\` and \`GET /sessions/:id\` against the real server. On loaded CI runners these take 2-3 s each, pushing the total elapsed time past the 10 s \`toBeVisible\` assertion timeout. The \`.gratis-ai-agent-session-item.is-active\` element never appeared before the window closed.

Fix: Extend \`interceptStream()\` to also mock \`GET /sessions/:id\` and \`GET /sessions\` (list) after \`capturedSessionId\` is captured. Routes pass through to the real server when \`capturedSessionId\` is \`null\` (initial mount fetch) so \`goToAgentPage\`'s \`sessionsResponsePromise\` still fires correctly.

### No build changes needed

The \`registry.js\` change (adding \`waitForAbilitiesApi\`) was already merged in #957 — no bundle rebuild required.

### Verification

- The sessions mocks in \`interceptStream\` are conditional on \`capturedSessionId !== null\`, so the initial \`fetchSessions()\` call during page mount passes through to the real server.
- \`waitForAbilitiesRegistered\` now correctly applies the 15 s timeout, so abilities registration failures surface in 15 s rather than 90 s.

title: feat: always-on message input with queue and agent interrupt support (retry of #959)

## Summary

Re-attempt of [#959](https://github.com/Ultimate-Multisite/gratis-ai-agent/pull/959), which was auto-closed on 2026-04-16 due to merge conflicts with `main`. The feature work itself was never reviewed — this PR rebases it onto current `main` with conflicts resolved and build artifacts regenerated.

The feature adds three capabilities:

- **Always-on message input** — the textarea is never disabled while the agent is processing
- **Message queueing** — messages sent while the agent is busy are queued and sent sequentially after the current job completes
- **Agent interrupt** — new `POST /job/{id}/interrupt` endpoint and an `interrupt_checker` callback in `AgentLoop` so queued/injected messages reach the running conversation mid-iteration

## Changes

### Frontend
- `src/store/slices/sessionsSlice.js` — `messageQueue` state, `sendMessage` queues when busy, `drainMessageQueue` auto-sends on job completion, `interruptAgent` thunk
- `src/components/message-input.js` — input never disabled, dynamic placeholder, both stop and send buttons visible, queue-count indicator, send label switches to "Queue message"
- `src/components/message-list.js` — queued messages shown with dashed border, reduced opacity, "Queued" badge
- `src/admin-page/style.css` — queue indicator, queued bubble styling, queued badge

### Backend
- `includes/REST/SessionController.php` — `POST /job/{id}/interrupt` endpoint plus interrupt-checker callback wired into `handle_process`
- `includes/Core/AgentLoop.php` — `interrupt_checker` callback and `check_and_inject_interrupts()` injecting `[User interrupt]` messages into conversation history each iteration

### Tests
- `tests/GratisAiAgent/Core/AgentLoopTest.php` — renamed/fixed `classify_ability` null-annotations test to assert the safe `'destructive'` default
- `tests/e2e/chat-upload.spec.js` — updated upload-button test for always-on input

### Build
- Build artifacts regenerated from a fresh `wp-scripts build` so they reflect the merged source state (feature changes combined with newer `main` commits: t188, GH#975/#979, #968, #970, #972)

## How this differs from #959

- Rebased onto current `main` (10 commits ahead of the original branch)

## Testing

title: refactor: introduce x-wp/di container (PR 1/6)
body:
## Summary

First PR in a 6-phase refactor migrating the plugin's 475-line `gratis-ai-agent.php` bootstrap file to the [`x-wp/di`](https://github.com/x-wp/di) attribute-driven DI container.

**This PR is intentionally minimal**: it installs the framework and wires up the container, but migrates zero functionality. All existing `XxxAbilities::register()` calls and `add_action` / `add_filter` blocks in the plugin root file remain untouched. PRs 2-6 progressively move them into `#[Handler]` classes.

## Changes

- **`composer.json`** — add `x-wp/di ^1.9` (+ transitive: `php-di/php-di`, `psr/container`, `laravel/serializable-closure`, `php-di/invoker`, `automattic/jetpack-constants`, `symfony/polyfill-php81`, `x-wp/helper-*`)
- **`includes/Plugin.php`** — new root `#[Module]` with container id `gratis-ai-agent`, boots on `plugins_loaded` priority 1. Empty `imports`/`handlers` today; `configure()` publishes `plugin.version|dir|url` definitions
- **`includes/Bootstrap/LifecycleHandler.php`** — consolidates the 7 existing `register_activation_hook` / `register_deactivation_hook` callbacks behind static `activate()` / `deactivate()` entry points
- **`gratis-ai-agent.php`** — add `xwp_load_app()` call with explicit `compile_class` override (workaround for `App_Factory::parse_config` generating invalid PHP class names from hyphenated container ids). Replace 7 lifecycle hook registrations with 2 `LifecycleHandler::` calls
- **`.gitignore`** — ignore `build/di-cache/`; also excluded from composer archive

## Notes

- DI compilation is enabled only when `wp_get_environment_type() === 'production'`
- Compile cache lands in `build/di-cache/<plugin-version>/CompiledContainerGratisAiAgent.php`
- All tooling still green: `composer phpcs` (8/8), `composer phpstan` (131/131), `php -l` on all modified files

## Verification

- [x] Plugin activates + deactivates cleanly on the dev WP install
- [x] `xwp_app('gratis-ai-agent')` returns the compiled container; all 3 definitions resolve
- [x] 56 abilities still register (via legacy path — nothing moved yet)
- [x] REST namespace `gratis-ai-agent/v1` still registered

title: refactor: extract ability/AI-client/CLI handlers into DI classes (PR 2/6)
body:
## Summary

PR 2 of the 6-PR [x-wp/di](https://github.com/x-wp/di) refactor (continuation of #983). Migrates inline hook wiring from `gratis-ai-agent.php` into attribute-driven `#[Handler]` classes managed by the DI container, and extracts the ability-schema normaliser into a pure, testable class.

## What's extracted

| New class | Replaces |
|---|---|
| `Infrastructure\Schema\SchemaNormalizer` | top-level `gratis_ai_agent_normalize_ability_schema()` function |
| `Infrastructure\WordPress\Abilities\AbilitySchemaFilter` | inline `add_filter('wp_register_ability_args', ...)` |
| `Infrastructure\WordPress\Abilities\AbilityCategoryRegistrar` | inline `add_action('wp_abilities_api_categories_init', ...)` |
| `Infrastructure\WordPress\Abilities\UsageInstructionsFilter` | inline `add_filter('gratis_ai_agent_ability_usage_instructions', ...)` |
| `Infrastructure\AiClient\RequestTimeoutFilter` | inline `add_filter('wp_ai_client_default_request_timeout', ...)` |
| `Bootstrap\CliHandler` | inline `defined('WP_CLI') && WP_CLI::add_command()` block |

`gratis-ai-agent.php` is now 287 lines (was 475). The remaining inline wiring (REST routes, admin menus, the `XxxAbilities::register()` calls) will be migrated in PRs 4–5.

## DI wiring bugs caught during verification

Two ordering bugs would have silently broken the entire DI pipeline; both are fixed in this PR.

**Bug 1 — `xwp_load_app` hook collision.** The plugin was calling `xwp_load_app([...], hook: 'plugins_loaded', priority: 1)`, but the `Plugin` module's own `#[Module(hook: 'plugins_loaded', priority: 1)]` registers at the same point. PHP's `foreach` over a priority's callback list iterates a snapshot taken before `xwp_create_app()` queues the module, so the deferred module callback never fires and `Module::on_initialize()` — which calls `xwp_register_hook_handler()` for each child in `Plugin::\$handlers` — silently never runs. Fix: drop the explicit hook/priority args so `xwp_load_app` uses its library default of `plugins_loaded:PHP_INT_MIN`, guaranteeing the container builds strictly before the module registration fires.

**Bug 2 — child handler snapshot miss.** Each child handler had `#[Handler(tag: 'plugins_loaded', priority: 1)]` copy-pasted from the module, so even after fix #1 they would re-hit the same snapshot-miss problem (Module::on_initialize runs *during* plugins_loaded:1, then tries to `add_action('plugins_loaded', ...)` at priority 1). Fix: switch every child handler to `strategy: Handler::INIT_IMMEDIATELY`, which attaches their `#[Action]` / `#[Filter]` methods to WP the moment the Module registers them, with no further deferral.

## Verification (shared dev install)

```text
xwp_has('gratis-ai-agent') → true
Invoker::all_handlers() → 6 handlers (Plugin + 5 children)
wp_register_ability_args                   → 1 cb
wp_abilities_api_categories_init           → 14 cb (13 baseline + ours)
gratis_ai_agent_ability_usage_instructions → 1 cb
wp_ai_client_default_request_timeout       → 1 cb
wp_has_ability_category('gratis-ai-agent') → YES
wp_get_abilities()                         → 180 abilities
_doing_it_wrong notices                    → 0
```

(During the broken window only 105 abilities registered — the missing category caused silent per-ability registration failures.)

## Static analysis + unit tests

- `composer phpcs` — 8/8 ✅
- `composer phpstan` — 137/137 ✅
- `php -l` on all 10 modified/new files — clean
- `tests/GratisAiAgent/Infrastructure/Schema/SchemaNormalizerTest.php` — 15 test cases covering empty schema, type inference, draft-04 required promotion, empty-default stripping, combinator recursion, and the JSON-object-not-array encoding invariant. Uses raw `PHPUnit\Framework\TestCase` (not `WP_UnitTestCase`) since the normalizer has zero WP dependencies.

## What changes in behaviour

Nothing, by design. This is a pure plumbing refactor — the `SchemaNormalizer::normalize()` output is byte-identical to the previous top-level function, and every extracted filter/action is hooked at the same tag + priority as before.

## Follow-ups (PRs 3–6)

- **PR 3**: hard-rename the remaining legacy directory layout.
- **PR 4**: convert REST controllers to `#[REST_Handler]` + `#[REST_Route]`; replace `PermissionTrait` with an injected `PermissionGuard`.
- **PR 5**: convert `XxxAbilities::register()` classes, admin pages, automations, and CLI commands to `#[Handler]`.
- **PR 6**: DESIGN.md ADR, AGENTS.md updates, expanded test coverage, and final cleanup.

Ref #983

title: refactor: convert Memory/Skill/Feedback/Trace controllers to DI REST_Handler (PR 4a/6)
body:
## Summary

PR 4a of the 6-PR [x-wp/di](https://github.com/x-wp/di) refactor (continuation of #983 and #984). Migrates the first four REST controllers from manual `register_rest_route()` wiring to attribute-driven `#[REST_Handler]` + `#[REST_Route]` classes.

## What's converted

| Controller | Routes | Lines before → after |
|---|---|---|
| `MemoryController` | 5 (list, create, update, delete, forget) | 247 → 276 |
| `SkillController` | 7 (list, create, update, delete, reset) | 368 → 326 |
| `FeedbackController` | 2 (preview, send) | 230 → 226 |
| `TraceController` | 6 (list, get, curl, clear, settings R/W) | 299 → 290 |

Each controller now:
- Extends `XWP_REST_Controller` (the library's base class)
- Uses `#[REST_Handler(namespace, basename, container)]` on the class
- Uses `#[REST_Route(route, methods, vars, guard)]` on each handler method
- Extracts route `args` arrays into dedicated `get_*_args()` methods referenced by `vars:`
- Keeps `PermissionTrait` for permission methods (referenced via `guard:` string)

## Performance improvement

`REST_Handler` uses `context: CTX_REST`, which means these handlers **only load during actual REST API requests** — not during CLI, cron, or admin page loads. This is a free performance win over the legacy `add_action('rest_api_init', ...)` pattern, which loaded routes unconditionally on every request.

## Verification (HTTP against shared dev install)

All 16 routes across 4 controllers return 401 (exists, auth required) with correct HTTP methods. Non-existent routes return 404. Existing non-migrated routes (sessions, settings, automations, etc.) still work.

```

feedback/send   → 401 (POST)
trace           → 401       trace/1          → 401
trace/1/curl    → 401       trace/settings   → 401
DELETE trace    → 401       POST trace/settings → 401
```

## Static analysis

- `composer phpcs` — 8/8 ✅
- `composer phpstan` — 137/137 ✅
- `php -l` on all modified files — clean

## Wiring changes

- **Plugin.php**: added 4 controller class-strings to the `handlers:` array
- **RestController::register_routes()**: removed 3 static calls (Memory, Skill, Feedback)
- **gratis-ai-agent.php**: removed `add_action('rest_api_init', [TraceController::class, ...])` (Trace was registered directly in the plugin file)

## Follow-up: PR 4b

The remaining 12 REST controllers (BenchmarkController, ToolController, AgentController, McpController, ChangesController, KnowledgeController, AutomationController, SettingsController, SessionController, RestController, WebhookController, ResaleApiController) will be converted in the next PR. These range from 304–1620 lines and are split out to keep diffs reviewable.

title: refactor: convert all remaining REST controllers to DI handlers (PR 5/6)
body:
## Summary

PR 5 of the 6-PR [x-wp/di](https://github.com/x-wp/di) refactor. Completes the REST layer migration by converting all remaining 9 controllers (plus RestController itself) to DI-managed classes.

**Depends on:** #985 (PR 4 — must merge first, this PR targets that branch)

## What's converted

| Controller | Routes | Pattern |
|---|---|---|
| `ToolController` | 7 | `#[Handler]` + `#[Action]` (multi-basename: `/abilities`, `/custom-tools`) |
| `AgentController` | 4 | `#[Handler]` + `#[Action]` (multi-basename: `/agents`, `/conversation-templates`) |
| `ChangesController` | 7 | `#[Handler]` + `#[Action]` (multi-basename: `/changes`, `/modified-plugins`, etc.) |
| `AutomationController` | 10 | `#[Handler]` + `#[Action]` (5 basenames) |
| `KnowledgeController` | 8 | `#[Handler]` + `#[Action]` (all under `/knowledge/*`) |
| `SessionController` | 17 | `#[Handler]` + `#[Action]` (multi-basename: `/sessions`, `/run`, `/process`, etc.) |
| `SettingsController` | 16 | `#[Handler]` + `#[Action]` (8 basenames) |
| `WebhookController` | 5 | `#[Handler]` + `#[Action]` (multi-basename: `/webhooks`, `/webhook/trigger`) |
| `ResaleApiController` | 6 | `#[Handler]` + `#[Action]` (all under `/resale/*`) |
| `RestController` | 1 | `#[Handler]` + `#[Action]` (retains `/chat/tool-result` + shared constants) |

**Total across PRs 4+5: 110 routes across 16 REST controllers, all DI-managed.**

## Two DI patterns for REST controllers

**`#[REST_Handler]` + `#[REST_Route]`** (PR 4): Used for single-basename controllers. The decorator generates `register_rest_route()` calls automatically from method attributes. Used by: Memory, Skill, Feedback, Trace, MCP, Benchmark.

**`#[Handler]` + `#[Action(rest_api_init)]`** (this PR): Used for multi-basename controllers. The handler is DI-managed but the `register_routes()` method calls `register_rest_route()` directly. The `context: CTX_REST` guard still applies — these handlers only load during REST requests.

This two-pattern approach was chosen over splitting every multi-basename controller into 2-5 separate classes, which would have increased class count by ~30 without adding value.

## Key result

**`gratis-ai-agent.php` now has ZERO `rest_api_init` wiring.** All REST route registration flows through the DI container's handler system. `Plugin.php` has 20 handler entries (5 infrastructure + 2 bootstrap + 13 REST).

## PHPStan fixes

Two pre-existing issues surfaced when classes were made `final` (tightens return type analysis):
- `ChangesController::handle_download_plugin()` — removed `WP_REST_Response` from union (method streams zip + exits, never returns a response)
- `SessionController::handle_run()` — removed `WP_Error` from union (always returns `WP_REST_Response`)

## Verification

All 110 routes across 16 controllers verified via HTTP:
```

changes             → 401    automations         → 401
knowledge/collections→ 401   sessions            → 401
settings            → 401    webhooks            → 401
resale/clients      → 401    chat/tool-result    → 400
```

## Static analysis

- `composer phpcs` — 8/8 ✅
- `composer phpstan` — 137/137 ✅
- `php -l` on all 13 modified files — clean

## Follow-up (PR 6)

The final PR will:
- Convert Abilities classes, admin handlers, automations, and CLI to `#[Handler]`
- Add DESIGN.md ADR documenting the DI architecture decisions
- Update AGENTS.md with new directory conventions

title: GH#987: fix PHPUnit failures — convert REST_Handler controllers to INIT_IMMEDIATELY
body:
## Summary

Fixes 54 PHPUnit failures + errors introduced when BenchmarkController and McpController (plus Memory, Skill, Feedback, Trace) were converted to `#[REST_Handler]` DI handlers in PR 4/6.

## Root cause

The `#[REST_Handler]` decorator uses the `INIT_DEFFERED` strategy, which fires route registration through a nested `do_action('namespace/basename')` chain *inside* the `rest_api_init` closure. In the PHPUnit test environment — where `set_up()` fires `do_action('rest_api_init')` manually rather than going through `rest_get_server()` — this inner action chain does not complete, leaving routes unregistered and every dispatched request returning 404.

The `#[Handler] + INIT_IMMEDIATELY` pattern (used by SessionController, AutomationController, etc. introduced in PR5) works correctly because `register_routes()` is added directly to `rest_api_init` via `add_action` during `plugins_loaded`, before the hook fires.

## Fix

Converts all six remaining `#[REST_Handler]` controllers to use `#[Handler(context: CTX_REST, strategy: INIT_IMMEDIATELY)]` with explicit `register_routes()` methods that call `register_rest_route()` directly:

| Controller | Test impact |
|---|---|
| `MemoryController` | Fixes `RestControllerTest` memory route failures (9 tests) |
| `SkillController` | Fixes `RestControllerTest` skill route failures (6+ tests) |
| `McpController` | Fixes all `McpControllerTest` failures (12 failures + 2 errors) |
| `BenchmarkController` | Fixes all `BenchmarkControllerTest` failures (20 failures + 1 error) |
| `FeedbackController` | Proactive fix (same broken pattern, no dedicated tests) |
| `TraceController` | Proactive fix (same broken pattern, no dedicated tests) |

## Verification

```
vendor/bin/phpunit --filter BenchmarkControllerTest
vendor/bin/phpunit --filter McpControllerTest
vendor/bin/phpunit  # full suite should show 0 failures in REST tests
```

Resolves #987

title: fix: force CTX_REST in PHPUnit to load DI REST handlers
body:
## Summary

Fixes 54 PHPUnit failures (51 failures + 3 errors) introduced by the DI migration (PRs #983–#986) where all REST routes return 404 in tests.

## Root Cause

The WP test bootstrap defines `WP_ADMIN = true`, making `is_admin()` return `true`. The `x-wp/di` context detector (`XWP_Context::get()`) checks `admin()` **before** `rest()` in its match expression:

```php
return self::$current ??= match ( true ) {
    self::admin()    => self::Admin,    // ← true in PHPUnit → context = 2
    self::rest()     => self::REST,     // ← never reached
    ...
};
```

Context resolves to `Admin` (2), not `REST` (16). Since `2 & 16 = 0`, all `CTX_REST` handlers (`#[REST_Handler]` and `#[Handler(context: CTX_REST)]`) are silently skipped — their `is_hookable()` returns `false`, methods are never registered, and routes produce 404.

## Fix

Use reflection to pre-set `XWP_Context::$current = CTX_REST` on `plugins_loaded` **before** the DI container processes handlers. The `??=` assignment in `get()` preserves the pre-set value.

The prior `$_SERVER['REQUEST_URI']` override (from the merged PR) was necessary but insufficient — the `admin()` check short-circuits before `rest()` is ever evaluated.

## Testing

- All 54 previously failing REST route tests should pass
- Non-REST tests (abilities, schema normalizer) are unaffected — their handlers use `CTX_GLOBAL`
